items.title: Rahul Gandhi Blames BJP for Connaught Place Shop Closures Amid Delhi Rally

items.summary: Two ancient ginkgo trees at Jinci Temple in Taiyuan, capital of Shanxi Province, northern China, have grown side by side for 500 years. Their trunks tower more than 20 meters tall and are so thick that two adults holding hands can barely wrap their arms around them. Visitors compare the pair to a devoted couple.
items.title: Ginkgo couple stands for half a millennium

items.summary: Swiss President Guy Parmelin is in China for a working visit from October 30 to November 1, the site states. The trip coincides with the two countries marking ten years of their strategic partnership. Talks are expected to focus on strengthening economic ties after negotiations concluded to upgrade their free trade agreement.
items.title: Swiss President Parmelin Opens Trade-Focused Visit to China

items.summary: The Guardian reports that weeks after its “one in, one out” removal scheme ended on 1 October, the Home Office is still chartering planes to return asylum seekers to France. The plan was announced by Emmanuel Macron and Keir Starmer in July 2025 to deter small boat crossings from northern France. Emma Ginn of Medical Justice said vulnerable people remain detained before forced removal. Freedom of information data suggests seven of the scheme’s 23 deportation flights were cancelled between July and September, more than double the prior year’s total. Home Office sources say returns continued after the deal ended. The Guardian also reports some returnees came back to the UK since 1 October while others wait in France. Evidence given by home secretary Shabana Mahmood indicates removals have cost at least £78m. Small boat crossings fell about 40% this year, matching a similar drop in irregular migration to Europe.
items.title: UK asylum returns to France continue after scheme ends

items.summary: Former chancellor Rachel Reeves argued in the Sunday Times that Britain's future lies within the European Union, saying Brexit has left it poorer, weaker and less secure. Writing after prime minister Andy Burnham's recent remarks drew questions about returning to the bloc or adopting its freedom of movement rules, she welcomed his leadership but stressed re-entry supporters must demonstrate tangible benefits.
items.title: Rachel Reeves backs Burnham as UK weighs EU re-entry path

items.summary: Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services (IL&FS) approached the Mumbai Bench of the National Company Law Tribunal seeking recovery of ₹185.88 crore in excess managerial remuneration paid to 23 former directors and those of subsidiaries IFIN and ITNL after financial statements were recast for FY14–FY18, which turned reported profits into a cumulative loss of ₹9,415.24 crore. IL&FS asked the tribunal for an interim direction requiring deposits in interest-bearing fixed accounts until the hearing. The company said only about 0.5 per cent has been refunded so far; former directors dispute that recast figures can invalidate audited original pay and call notices vague.
items.title: IL&FS Seeks Tribunal Recovery of ₹185.88 Crore From Former Directors

items.summary: During festive season, Indian automobile manufacturers reported record vehicle dispatches in October. Maruti Suzuki India sold 2,76,120 units including exports, its highest-ever monthly volume, with domestic wholesales of 2,16,789 units up 20 per cent year-on-year from 1,80,675 units. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles recorded 73,894 domestic wholesales, a 21 per cent rise; Mahindra & Mahindra sold 73,338 vehicles, plus 2 per cent growth. Hyundai Motor India reached an all-time high of 82,299 total units with 17.
items.title: Indian Automakers Post Record October Vehicle Sales Amid Festive Demand

items.summary: Thousands of Filipinos visited cemeteries across Manila on Sunday (Nov 1) for Undas, a tradition blending Catholic observances with pre-colonial ancestor veneration. Interviewees offered flowers, candles and sticky rice cakes while sharing memories of their departed relatives. Anthropology lecturer Nestor Castro noted that Filipino family reunions during funerals strengthen kinship bonds, reflecting customs shared across other Catholic countries.
items.title: Filipinos Honor the Dead on All Saints' Day

items.summary: Turkey moved Abdullah Ocalan, leader of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), to a newly built section of his island prison on Imrali as part of peace efforts. A senior Kurdish official, Mithat Sancar, confirmed the relocation in an interview with Medya Haber TV without further details. He said the move “necessitates an acceleration of the (peace) process.” The 42-year conflict has killed tens of thousands since 1984. Ocalan remains influential among Kurds and is seen as key to advancing talks, though he must coordinate negotiations rather than act unilaterally.
items.title: Turkey Relocates Ocalan Within Imrali Prison Amid Peace Efforts

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported in its latest bulletin that cyclone 'Murasu' has formed over the Bay of Bengal and is likely to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast by November 3. The system, named by India, could intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur by morning of November 3. Odisha's government has announced a high alert in the southern region and ordered evacuation from low-lying areas, while meteorological officials expect rainfall beginning November 2 with intensifying intensity on November 3 and 4.
items.title: India's IMD Confirms Formation of Cyclone Murasu Over Bay of Bengal

items.summary: Terence Atmane admitted struggling with his mental health after an outburst at the Shanghai Masters, in which he threw his racket toward the stands and narrowly missed striking fans. He apologized publicly for a sharp ranking drop to the edge of the top 100. The incident highlighted pressures lower-ranked players face as another demanding season draws to a close.
items.title: Lower-ranked tennis players face mental strain near season's end

items.summary: Households in the West Midlands told the BBC they welcome a £100 household energy payment announced by Chancellor John Healey, but worry it will not go far enough over winter. Personal accountant Kelly Birkett said the sum gets absorbed into other costs and leaves families no better off, while coach driver Mark Sumner described falling into 'energy debt'. The government says millions of families benefit from wider measures.
items.title: West Midlands families want energy bill help revisited after Budget

items.summary: The Diwali Foundation brought hundreds of volunteers together at an event in Hockley, where about 300 people turned up to pack food parcels. The charity said it has provided around 23,470 food hampers so far and set a target of providing 6,000 this year. Volunteers and housing group staff described the cost of living crisis as ongoing while praising the support offered to struggling families.
items.title: Diwali Foundation volunteers pack food hampers for Birmingham families

items.summary: Security professionals are warning people to keep their date of birth private after a hack at retailer Asos exposed customers' details. Jake Moore of ESET says dates of birth help criminals commit identity fraud when combined with other data. Alexandre François found eight out of 14 retailers he surveyed asked for the information on sign-up, noting shops have little incentive to remove it.
items.title: Cybersecurity experts warn against sharing birthdays online

items.summary: A shelter introduces Cassiopeia and Galaxy, a black-and-white tuxedo kitten named Galaxy and an all-black brother weighing over 5 kilograms nicknamed Big Boy. Born around May 2025, the pair were among four kittens found by a kind soul who brought them to ARK in April. The siblings are deeply attached and must be adopted together as a showcase pair.
items.title: Adorable Feline Siblings Await Loving Homes Together

items.summary: Ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, the article notes that left-wing parties won majorities in both Serbia and Brazil. Foreign policy analyst Lawrence J. Haas says these results are bad news for President Donald Trump but will not affect the midterms. In Serbia, outgoing president Aleksandar Vucic lost an ally; in Brazil, incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Jair Bolsonaro's camp. After losing, Flavio Bolsonaro fled to Florida and claimed the vote was rigged, echoing Trump's own remarks that it 'looked like another rigged election.' With Trump at his lowest midterm approval rating since 1946, analysts warn of difficult prospects ahead.
items.title: Trump Loses Allies After Elections in Serbia and Brazil

items.summary: A suburban Chicago man was sentenced to two years in federal prison for conspiring to stage armed robberies so victims could apply for immigration visas. From 2022 to 2024, PARTH NAYI organized hundreds of staged robberies at stores and gas stations nationwide, recruiting fake victims who paid $5,000 to $30,000 each to pose as robbery victims and file fraudulent U-Visa applications with Citizenship and Immigration Services.
items.title: Chicago Man Sentenced for Staged Robberies to Secure Fake U-Visas

items.summary: Xiaomi said on Sunday it delivered more than 50,000 electric vehicles in October, its highest monthly total of the year. The company cited ramping production to reach a 2026 target of 550,000 vehicles, which January–October deliveries at about 336,000 units—roughly 61 per cent of that goal—still fall short of.
items.title: Xiaomi Hits Record October EV Deliveries Above 50,000

items.summary: Hartmut Jenner, CEO of German cleaning-equipment maker Kärcher, warns that Germany and Europe risk deindustrialisation amid a "perfect storm" in the economic situation. Writing an exclusive opinion piece for Euronews, he points to unpredictable US trade policy raising tariffs without warning, China's aggressive technological competition backed by state subsidies, and heavy bureaucracy as threats to investment-oriented companies. Jenner, who has led Kärcher since 2001 and tripled staff and turnover in that time, calls for cuts in red tape, incentives for extra work, and a firm EU trade policy towards the US and China. He describes Germany's forecast growth of 1.3% as "borrowed growth" driven by debt rather than real recovery. Kärcher, founded in 1935 with headquarters in Winnenden, generated almost €3.5 billion turnover in 2025, earning 86% abroad across 87 countries and employing 17,000 people worldwide. He urges a cultural shift toward pragmatism and personal responsibility to restore competitiveness. (149 words)
items.title: Kärcher CEO Warns Europe Faces Economic Perfect Storm

items.summary: Jet fuel for domestic airlines rose Rs 1.3 per litre, the fourth consecutive monthly increase, PTI reported on Sunday, bringing aviation turbine fuel to Rs 138.5 from Rs 137.1 a litre. The Hindu said commercial LPG prices also climbed about Rs 10 per 19-kg cylinder nationwide, marking its third straight rise. Airlines cite higher global oil costs and airspace restrictions after the West Asia conflict as drivers of rising operating expenses.
items.title: India raises jet fuel and commercial LPG prices amid regional conflict

items.summary: Prateek Agrawal of Motilal Oswal AMC, speaking at the ET Wealth Expo in Mumbai on Saturday (2024), advised long-term investors to focus on growth investing rather than market volatility. He suggested shortlisting two fund managers and combining both styles into a focused portfolio of around 30 stocks plus value holdings reaching about 100 total. Agrawal noted that holding multiple portfolios can create overlapping exposure, while his firm's approach uses high conviction across roughly 30 names. He also discussed momentum investing through its Active Momentum Fund and flagged how taxes could cut retained returns by close to 2% when markets compound at 15% with a 12.5% charge on gains (s44). His views are his own, per The Economic Times disclaimer.
items.title: Motilal Oswal's Agrawal Advises Focused Growth Investing for Long-Term Investors

items.summary: A US Senate race in Texas has become the most expensive in history, with total spending exceeding half a billion dollars. Democrats hope James Talarico could win it for his party since 1988, after decades of losing statewide races. His lead remains near the margin of error in polls, and Republicans warn that a Democratic breakthrough could trigger wider losses across Texas and nationally. Campaign donations from Elon Musk alone surpassed $170m, while Talarico raised more than $140m overall. Brendan Steinhauser called it 'a perfect storm' for Democrats. The outcome remains uncertain amid last-minute turnout appeals from Trump supporters.
items.title: Talarico's Texas Senate Bid Could Flip a Blue Seat

items.summary: Hundreds of high street “slot farms” could keep claiming a leisure-business business rates discount by holding bingo licences despite running slot machines almost exclusively, Guardian analysis suggests. The government raised duty on slot takings from 20% to 25%. Officials say adult gaming centres and vape shops in England will lose the discount. A Labour MP urged vigilance over licensing loopholes; a real estate expert said business rates treatment may hinge on how an AGC is defined.
items.title: Slot farms may dodge budget tax via bingo loophole

items.summary: Several French fuel retailers lowered pump prices following a government release of ten million barrels from strategic stocks, purchased before the Middle East war and sold at 0.28 euro per litre versus an average of 1.1 euro in mid-October. TotalEnergies reduced Access station diesel to 2.15 euros per litre; E.Leclerc cut prices by 21 cents across roughly 742 stations, deducted daily while remaining tied to market movements; Coopérative U will match the reduction. Prices remain subject to market fluctuations.
items.title: French retailers cut diesel prices after tapping strategic reserves

items.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs announced on Saturday that IPS officer Sandeep Chaudhary, who led the National Investigation Agency’s probe into the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, received the Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak in the investigation category. The award is given annually to recognise excellent work across roughly 490 personnel honoured for 2026. PTI reported that the MHA’s published list did not identify the specific case behind his selection. Chaudhary, a 2012-batch NIA Deputy Inspector General of the AGMUT cadre, was among 123 officers recognised for investigative work and had been promoted to DIGP effective 1 January.
items.title: IPS Officer Chaudhary Awarded Medal for Pahalgam Probe

items.summary: Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar chaired the INDIA bloc's public impeachment proceedings against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in a setting resembling Parliament, held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. The iconic chair had once been occupied by Jawaharlal Nehru, per Pawan Khera of Congress's media wing, who posted an image on X and said the seat carried Nehru's legacy. Opposition MPs passed a resolution declaring Kumar unfit, accusing him of deleting votes to steal elections and demanding he be tried for treason.
items.title: ‘Nehru’s Chair’ takes focus as Meira Kumar leads 'public impeachment' proceedings | In Photo

items.summary: Supermodel and TV host Heidi Klum attended her annual costume party on 31 October, dressing as a giant, bloodied severed hand. At 53, she said the look was her own chopped-off left hand, making her unrecognisable. The event marked its 25th anniversary, having produced viral moments such as her worm costume in 2022.
items.title: Heidi Klum Appears as Giant Severed Hand at Halloween Party

items.summary: A pedestrian died at a crash on Sunday morning near Salisbury North, in Adelaide's northern suburbs, where emergency services responded to an intersection of Waterloo Corner Road and Whites Road. A second pedestrian was hospitalized with serious injuries. The uninjured driver has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving and will appear in the Elizabeth Magistrates Court on December 14.
items.title: Driver charged after pedestrian death in Adelaide crash

items.summary: The Sensex rose 308 points to close near 74,460 and the Nifty 50 advanced 116 points to settle at 23,053 after Friday's session. Broader indices faced selling pressure, with midcap and smallcap benchmarks declining up to 2%. Analysts VK Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments Ltd and Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities outlined factors investors will watch: oil volatility amid geopolitical events; foreign inflows as FIIs turned net buyers worth Rs 6,305 crore after a 10-week selling streak; the rupee's best monthly gain in eight months to close at 94.95 against the dollar; and continued weakness across midcap and smallcap indices.
items.title: Indian indices rally as investors weigh four factors on Monday

items.summary: All information is sourced from publishers, who describe six new Indian fiction titles arriving for the festive season: two short-story collections and four novels. Tanuj Solanki's Appropriation: Stories spans interpersonal drama to political satire; Rakshanda Jalil's The Aunts of Gangapur follows a woman escaping Delhi smog to her husband's ancestral home in Gangapur; Imayam's Heartwreck, translated by GJV Prasad, concerns an affair interrupted by the lover's wife Kamatchi; Vish Dhamija's Showtime! is a Mumbai murder mystery spanning twenty years; Onkar Bulbule's The Haveli of Kalipur follows psychiatrist Raghav into a haunted house; and N Prabhakaran's A Fistful of Salt gathers stories from his career, which began in 1971 across more than 50 books.
items.title: Indian publishers offer two story collections and four novels for November

items.summary: In Australia's women's rugby league World Cup match against Wales, the Jillaroos won 124-6. The result set a new record as the biggest margin in women's international history and included Jesse Southwell scoring 44 points alone. Writer Andrew Argyle argues that despite this dominance, the blowout served no competitive purpose: it damaged the tournament's credibility, offered nothing for player development, and handed ammunition to critics of women's sport. He notes Wales played well enough to earn a cheer from the sparse crowd but was overwhelmed by an Australian side considered dominant 'by an order of magnitude.' Argyle concludes that total obliteration leaves no legacy beyond being a historical oddity.
items.title: Australia's latest World Cup smash-up helps nobody

items.summary: The INDIA bloc staged a large opposition rally at Ramlila Maidan, New Delhi, drawing Congress, Samajwadi Party and Left supporters who filled the venue to capacity. Speakers stressed protecting constitutional voting rights amid Election Commission concerns over the Special Intensive Revision process. The crowd reportedly exceeded 50,000 people, causing road spillover. Analysts noted electoral impact would depend on addressing core issues rather than symbolic messaging.
items.title: INDIA Bloc Rally Draws Large Opposition Turnout in Delhi

items.summary: The Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple administration placed junior electrical engineer S Janakiraman under temporary suspension, effective October 31, over a two-minute power blackout during Vice President C P Radhakrishnan's visit on October 30. The order cites carelessness and was signed by R Rukmani; charges were filed under Section 56(1) of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act of 1959, with a 15-day window to respond and 30 days for an appeal.
items.title: Engineer Suspended Over Blackout During VP's Madurai Temple Visit

items.summary: Indian smartphone maker Lava plans to increase the price of some models by as much as Rs 3,000 starting November 15, 2026. The company cites memory shortages and industry challenges for the move, which mainly affects budget and mid-range buyers under Rs 30,000.
items.title: नया स्मार्टफोन खरीदने वालों को झटका! Lava के फोन ₹3,000 तक होंगे महंगे, कंपनी ने बता दी तारीख

items.summary: The INDIA bloc organised a large rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, drawing supporters from Congress, Samajwadi Party and the Left. Leaders including Rahul Gandhi attended in an open vehicle to project unity ahead of electoral contests. The Bharatiya Janata Party staged counter-protests across Rohtak, Shimla and Lucknow over 1984 anti-Sikh riots. Alliance members countered BJP trade-disruption claims by saying visiting supporters would boost local businesses.
items.title: INDIA Bloc Ramlila Rally Draws Crowds as BJP Stages Counter-Protests

items.summary: A new analysis by the McKinsey Global Institute, published on October 21, 2026, highlights a growing disconnect between America's booming technology investments and its wider industrial economy. According to McKinsey, hyperscaler R&D and capital expenditure rose 50-fold from around $15 billion in 2005 to $750 billion in 2025, potentially approaching $1 trillion by the end of 2026. Yet productive investment as a share of US GDP has barely changed, factory structures declined 6% by the end of 2025 after peaking in 2024, and manufacturing costs remain roughly 40% higher for semiconductors than abroad. McKinsey argues that modular construction and AI-driven systems could close part of the gap but cannot alone guarantee industrial resurgence.
items.title: US AI Spending Fails to Spark Industrial Revival

items.summary: In Punjab's Patiala district, two Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) members of the Legislative Assembly resigned from primary membership on Sunday. Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra left a day after AAP released its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections. The party has not yet named candidates in either constituency.
items.title: Two AAP MLAs Resign After First Candidate List Announcement

items.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw flagged off the inaugural Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express on Sunday, strengthening overnight rail connectivity between the two cities. The 16-coach rake departed Sir M Visvesvaraya Terminal at 7.45 pm and is scheduled to reach Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus Mumbai at 6.15 am Monday, per officials. Regular services begin November 2 in one direction and November 3 in the other.
items.title: Railway Minister Flags Off Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express

items.summary: The Aubrey Independent School District in Texas named a new elementary school after Marilyn Hampton, a custodian who worked for 39 years. On October 21, officials announced the honour at a board of trustees meeting where superintendent Shannon Saylor asked Hampton to unroll a red carpet; when she opened it, her name appeared on it. The district had not told her beforehand and initially invited her under the impression she was discussing another matter. Hampton said she could not speak from emotion. The building, previously Elementary School Number Five, is scheduled to open in August 2027.
items.title: Texas School District Names New Elementary Building After Long-Term Custodian

items.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered Sunday at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi for a protest led by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and backed by the youth Cockroach movement, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter list revisions critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party. The review has removed more than 130 million names since last year. Human Rights Watch called it unfair; the commission denies the claims.
items.title: Opposition Parties Rally in New Delhi Demanding Election Chief Resignation

items.summary: Newly released nationwide figures show Vietnam sold more than 3 million motorcycle and scooter units in the first nine months of 2026, up 25.9% over the same period last year. The electric segment surged 90.5% to 973,247 units, now roughly 32% of all new sales. VinFast rose to second place with a 152.1% increase, ahead of Honda’s modest 8.4% growth and Yamaha in third. Government plans to restrict gasoline motorcycles in parts of Hanoi are cited as part of the shift.
items.title: Vietnam Electric Two-Wheeler Sales Overtake Gasoline Growth as VinFast Surges Past Honda

items.summary: Hundreds of supporters cheered Cape Verde President Jose Maria Neves at a rally in Sao Vicente on Saturday, marking the start of presidential election campaigning. Neves is seeking a second term in the November 15 vote and is backed by PAICV, which won May's legislative elections. Six candidates are running ahead of an official campaign end on November 13.
items.title: Cape Verde President Rallies Supporters as Campaigning Kicks Off

items.summary: As Andhra Pradesh moves ahead with local body elections, the disputed Kotia Gram Panchayat on the Odisha border has become a flashpoint in a 70-year territorial row. Twenty-one of the panchayat's 28 villages are claimed by both states; Odisha says they lie in Koraput district while Andhra places them under Parvathipuram Manyam. With no joint survey ever settling their status, Odisha has filed a contempt petition accusing Andhra of violating a 2006 Supreme Court order that left the boundary to Parliament and told both sides to maintain the status quo. Revenue minister Suresh Pujari ordered close monitoring as police set up checkpoints in six villages. More than 5,000 residents hold cards from both states while clashes flare each election season.
items.title: Andhra polls trigger Odisha court fight over Kotia border villages

items.summary: Lewis Hamilton took his first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City, marking his first since July 2023 and making him the oldest pole-sitter since Mario Andretti in 1982. Comparing himself to Michael Schumacher's early years with Ferrari, Hamilton said watching Schumacher was special. Sunday looks set to crown Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli as Formula One's youngest champion at 20, needing a top-nine finish.
items.title: Hamilton's Ferrari Pole Recalls Schumacher as Antonelli Eyes Title

items.summary: Gross GST collections rose 23 per cent to over Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, government data released on Sunday (November 1) showed. The total combined Central GST of 42,935 crore, State GST of Rs 51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over Rs 1.37 lakh crore. Growth was driven by strong mop-up from domestic sales, which rose 16 per cent to over Rs 1.59 lakh crore, and imports, up 42 per cent to Rs 72,246 crore. GST refunds climbed 6.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 27,934 crore; after adjusting for them, net collections rose 26 per cent to over Rs 2.03 lakh crore.
items.title: Government GST mop-up swelled October collections by a fifth

items.summary: An engineer who studies human factors and transportation safety says automated trucks are unlikely to replace drivers soon. Companies like Torc have tested early models on limited routes in Texas and California, with simulations suggesting benefits such as improved safety, fuel economy, reduced parking needs, lower emissions from idling, and help easing the driver shortage. However, challenges remain around variable weather, changing road conditions, unpredictable human drivers, and whether people should stay inside cabs.
items.title: Expert Says Driverless Trucks Face Real Roadblocks Before Widespread Use

items.summary: A major fire broke out Sunday at a plastic packaging warehouse in Wardhaman Nagar, Nagpur, spreading rapidly due to large quantities of stored raw materials. Six to seven fire engines brought the blaze under control with no casualties reported; cause is undetermined. Separately, Saturday night's steam boiler explosion at Chemfield Company in Kalmeshwar MIDC injured three workers—Neeraj Yadav, Ravi Nishad and 18-year-old June Banding—who were later discharged after hospital treatment.
items.title: Nagpur Warehouse Fire and Boiler Explosion Raise Safety Concerns

items.summary: Former BJP president JP Nadda accused Rahul Gandhi and the INDIA bloc of attempting to create unrest with their November 1 Ramlila Maidan rally, calling it a conspiracy to plunge India into anarchy. Nadda described the protest as an orchestrated drama by rejected parties and outlined what he termed a four-stage 'anarchy model' involving spreading lies, inciting chaos, damaging the economy, and destabilising government at foreign powers' behest.
items.title: JP Nadda accuses Rahul Gandhi of anarchy model at Ramlila rally

items.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party, founded by Abhijeet Dipke, says it supports the INDIA bloc's Sunday, November 1 rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities and demands his resignation. Dipke explained that while the party stands in solidarity, it will not join the protest to preserve its independent identity as a neutral platform. Banerjee acknowledged the CJP's backing, calling them pioneers of the movement.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party backs INDIA bloc rally but declines protest

items.summary: On 1 November 2026, the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder in Delhi rose by ₹10 to ₹2,820. This marks the third consecutive monthly increase for commercial LPG, while domestic rates stay unchanged at ₹942 per 14.2-kg cylinder. The hikes follow October's ₹62.50 rise and September's ₹9.50 gain, with prices having peaked at ₹3,113.50 in June before declining.
items.title: Delhi Commercial LPG Prices Rise Rs 10 From November

items.summary: A Quartz article reports that Redfin's data show a broad pullback in U.S. homebuying, framed as 10 signs of weakening demand from Seattle to Las Vegas. The central figure is pending home sales at 281,749 seasonally adjusted for the four weeks ending Oct. 18, 2026, Redfin's lowest level since records began in 2021 and 14.4% below a year earlier. Pending sales fell across all 50 most populous metros tracked, marking the second consecutive week of universal declines. Mortgage rates averaged 7.4%, lifting the median monthly payment to $2,796, up 10.4%. Among five steepest-pending-sales metros, Seattle led with a 28.8% drop and also posted its largest price decline at 6.2%; San Diego fell 25.4%, Atlanta 23.8% alongside new listings down 24.2%, Denver 21%, and Las Vegas 20.6%. Nationally, new listings hit a three-month low of 354,412 while active listings rose to 1,507,161 with months of supply at 4.4. Redfin's report gives no local causes for the declines; figures are subject to revision and its series begins in 2021, excluding earlier downturns like the 2008 slump.
items.title: Redfin flags sinking U.S. homebuyer demand across major metros

items.summary: Anmol N Jain’s Swarajya Sunday Digest opens with B L Santhosh, the BJP general secretary, describing how his party covered only visible goals like the Ram temple while leaving decolonisation unseen. The piece notes the BJP trained more than 48,000 block-level councillors after Covid and cites Uttar Pradesh results where SP-Congress led in 229 of 403 seats versus 174 for BJP allies. It also touches on Chinese firms bidding for Indian tenders without checks, India’s Rs 23,800 crore import of testing instruments in 2024-25, and the Bihar Museum rising to ninth among the world’s best. The digest closes eight pieces as worth a Sunday read.
items.title: Swarajya Sunday Digest Frames BJP’s Hidden Agenda and India’s Unseen Work

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports a Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California with no crash involved, closing southbound lanes for nearly ten hours. This marks the second such highway shutdown by an electric semi in just over two years; the first occurred in August 2024 near Emigrant Gap and required 50,000 gallons of water plus a 15-hour closure. The outlet argues fire is not unique to EVs—diesel trucks catch fire roughly 40 times daily—but lithium packs sustain thermal runaway that is far harder to extinguish. It notes the tiny Tesla Semi pilot fleet makes failure rates statistically unreliable and points to legacy builders like Volvo, whose recalls stem from a century of safety systems versus Silicon Valley's faster but less battle-tested approach.
items.title: Tesla Semi Fires Reveal EV Trucking's Experience Gap

items.summary: Zahoor Ahad Tantray, general secretary of the Kashmir Fruit Growers and Dealers Association, says Grade A apples face strong demand during Diwali. However, he warns that supplies in fruit mandis are inadequate because apple scab spread widely this year, lowering quality significantly.
items.title: Kashmir Apple Supply Falls Short of Diwali Demand

items.summary: Union Labour & Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched EPFO services through a verified WhatsApp channel, letting subscribers check PF balances, recent transactions and passbooks without visiting offices. On EPFO's 74th Foundation Day he also introduced automatic settlement for eligible inoperative accounts with Aadhaar verification and balances up to Rs 1,000, expected to help about one lakh accounts worth Rs 5 crore. A labour ministry statement reported the rollout; Mandaviya noted the Rs 32 lakh crore corpus from more than 8 crore members. PTI is the source. He urged worker-centric innovations ahead of EPFO's 75th year.
items.title: Mandaviya Launches EPFO Services on WhatsApp and Auto Settlements

items.summary: At a Nov 1 online meeting, seven core OPEC+ members kept their December oil output targets steady. The group faces continued export disruptions from the US-Iran war and is expected to decide its 2027 production framework at a ministerial meeting on Nov 29. Analysts say the review must account for uncertainty over the conflict, recovery through the Strait of Hormuz, and returning barrels.
items.title: OPEC+ Holds December Oil Targets Amid Iran War Disruptions

items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says his thinking on AI alignment has changed over the past 12 months. He recalled that in 2018 and 2019, when Dario Amodei, Ilya Sutskever, Sam Altman, Greg Brockman and Elon Musk were one happy family, he believed scaling laws would make alignment fall out naturally. Now he says alignment may be a harder problem than previously assumed.
items.title: Nadella Revises AI Alignment View After PHP Security Crisis

items.summary: Nearly one in five private homes resold in Singapore’s prime location market ended in a loss in the third quarter, according to data compiled for The Business Times by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield (C&W). Islandwide, loss-making deals rose to 4.6% from 3.7% previously and 3.3% a year earlier – the highest proportion since Q2 2022’s 6.9%. Of 2,021 matched transactions, 93 sold at a loss; CCR accounted for half (49%), with OCR at 20%. Overall profit margins shrank to a median gain of 24.8%, down from 30.4% in Q2 2025.
items.title: Singapore Prime-Region Home Resales Sold at a Loss in Q3

items.summary: Ahead of Diwali, demand for Kashmiri apples remained strong in terminal markets across the country, but supplies lagged after a scab outbreak damaged much of this year's crop. Zahoor Ahad Tantray, general secretary of the Kashmir Fruit Growers and Dealers Association, said more Grade B and C fruit was reaching mandis because quality deteriorated significantly; he estimated that around 50 to 55 per cent or up to 60 per cent arriving were low-grade apples with weak demand.
items.title: Kashmiri Apple Supplies Fall Short of Diwali Demand Amid Scab Outbreak

items.summary: A US investigation into alleged diversion of advanced AI chips and sensitive commercial information centers on Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le. The New York Times reports she had close contacts with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia denies sharing sensitive trade secrets, calling meetings routine business activity.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Allegations Over AI Chip Diversion Tied to Chinese Businesswoman Alice Huang

items.summary: Mumbai Police arrested Mohammed Sabir Mohammed Rustam, a tailor from Vasai East and Meerut, for allegedly secretly filming women on suburban trains and morphing their images with AI before posting them on Instagram reels. He reportedly used a fake profile to gain views while boarding the general compartment next to the ladies' coach. His phone was seized; investigators are probing possible commercial use.
items.title: Mumbai Man Arrested For Secretly Filming Women On Trains

items.summary: Union Labour & Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched EPFO's WhatsApp service on the organisation's 74th Foundation Day, letting subscribers view their provident fund balance, recent transactions and passbook details. Subscribers with Aadhaar-verified inoperative accounts holding balances up to Rs 1,000 will no longer file individual claims; EPFO will settle them automatically after identity and bank-account verification. Mandaviya said about one lakh such accounts worth Rs 5 crore are expected to benefit.
items.title: EPFO Launches WhatsApp Service for PF Balance Checks and Auto-Settlement of Small Accounts

items.summary: The Ministry of Manpower replied to a letter from Tan Teck We, who wrote 'Still looking for work, but outside the safety net' on 20 October. The writer described job seekers spending many months searching, interviewing and retraining as taking a heavy financial and emotional toll. In response, the ministry pointed to the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme, which offers temporary aid to lower- to middle-income involuntarily unemployed persons so they need not rush into ill-fitting jobs. For those facing longer unemployment, assistance is based on household needs rather than employment history, with options including ComCare, Social Service Offices and HDB for housing-loan servicing.
items.title: Singapore Responds to Long-Term Unemployed Job Seeker's Appeal for Financial Support Beyond Employment History

items.summary: Raymond Lim raises concerns that upgrading works at seniors' fitness corners often run long contracts without matching work progress, leaving sites fenced off with little activity. He notes residents rely on these spaces for exercise and social contact, so prolonged closures disrupt daily routines. He urges town councils to keep facilities open until contractors are ready and avoid unnecessary idle time.
items.title: Senior fitness corner upgrades need better project management

items.summary: A column argues that calm over the US-China trade war is misleading, as both sides pursue supply-chain dominance framed as a national security priority. China throttled rare earth and magnet exports last year to retaliate against tariffs and semiconductor restrictions; it has relaxed some controls but keeps many. The International Energy Agency estimated blocking access to rare earth magnets could cost the US and Europe about $1.5tn per year. Washington is funding mining projects and restricting advanced tech, while China announced export limits on AI chips and solar technology. The author warns that interdependence has become a vulnerability and predicts the odds of lasting peace are slim.
items.title: Supply chain rivalry risks reigniting US-China trade conflict

items.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said Sunday that India has held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on protecting civilian shipping, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure amid the ongoing war. Speaking at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, he stressed bringing parties together to find common ground.
items.title: Jaishankar Calls for Russia, Ukraine and Europe Talks on Three Conflict Fronts

items.summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra mocked the opposition's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan as a 'super flop,' claiming around 40% of the ground was empty. He accused Congress leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, of using camera angles to exaggerate turnout and questioned where the expected 10 lakh people were. The venue has a capacity of 50,000.
items.title: BJP Calls INDIA Bloc Ramlila Maidan Rally a Super Flop

items.summary: The page lists selected remarks by Chinese President Xi Jinping on building a community with a shared future in cyberspace ahead of the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, held Monday to Thursday in Zhejiang Province. The vision dates from his 2015 opening address and has been promoted for over a decade amid new artificial intelligence developments.
items.title: Xi's key quotes on a shared future in cyberspace

items.summary: Foreign investors turned net buyers toward the end of October, infusing around Rs 6,300 crore during October 26-30 versus outflows of nearly Rs 2,700 crore a week earlier. Cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities in 2026 reached Rs 2.95 lakh crore. Experts caution that one week of buying may not signal sustained reversal.
items.title: FPIs Turn Net Buyers in Late October as Outflows Ease

items.summary: The China Manned Space Agency says work is progressing steadily across all tasks in the lunar-landing phase of the country's lunar exploration program. In a Saturday video, it outlined upcoming missions including a Long March 10 rocket verification flight, first flights of the Mengzhou crewed spacecraft and Lanyue lunar lander, plus the Chang'e 7 mission. The China Space Station will open to scientists worldwide.
items.title: China Manned Space Agency Reports Steady Lunar-Landing Progress

items.summary: A two-day G20 foreign ministers' meeting ended in Atlanta on October 31, 2026 without a joint communique. Participants failed to reach consensus on major geopolitical and economic security issues amid the Ukraine crisis and US-Iran conflict. Chaired by Marco Rubio, who noted reporters solutions remain elusive, delegates stayed divided over the Ukraine crisis, US-Iran tensions and tariffs.
items.title: G20 Foreign Ministers End Meeting Without Joint Communique Amid Deep Divisions

items.summary: Betsi Cadwaladr University health board, which serves about a quarter of Wales’s population, said it was consulting on ending urgent primary care centres (UPCCs) at Ysbyty Penrhos Stanley in Holyhead, Ysbyty Alltwen in Tremadog and Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor by April 2027. Local MPs warned of “dire consequences,” while the board’s chief executive said access to urgent care remained a priority.
items.title: Welsh Health Board Considers Closing Urgent Care Centres Amid Criticism

items.summary: John Healey’s debut UK budget may be remembered for introducing PDEL, or preventative departmental expenditure limit, a new category designed to protect funding for children, youth and rough sleeping. The Treasury intends departments to justify individual projects as preventive ahead of an IFS-described “brutal” spending review next year. Demos argued that £22bn in costs could have been averted through prevention, while the Nuffield Foundation’s Gavin Kelly noted better data now links services more clearly. However, based on figures set out in the budget, the IFS reckons £27bn-worth of spending pressures remain next year.
items.title: UK budget introduces PDEL for preventive spending

items.summary: China's electric vehicle automaker Geely has announced it is entering the Canadian auto market, targeting 2027. The company states that it has assembled a local team and begun building out a retail and service network. This move follows an earlier agreement between Canada and China to allow 49,000 Chinese EV exports to Canada this year.
items.title: Geely Auto Group Plans Canadian Market Entry in 2027

items.summary: Bayern Munich said on Sunday that Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry were ruled out for an indefinite period after both left Saturday's 2-2 Bundesliga draw with Borussia Dortmund. Saibari suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his right ankle joint and has already undergone successful surgery, leaving him on crutches. Gnabry sustained a muscle injury in his posterior left thigh, confirmed shortly after being substituted.
items.title: Bayern Rule Out Saibari and Gnabry Indefinitely

items.summary: The article lists provisional candidates for poorly reasoned posts from an archive of 40,326 downloaded posts, clarifying that this is not an objective ranking. It examines five reviews by Tyler Cowen and Alex Tabarrok, identifying recurring defects: certainty exceeding the argument, uncharitable treatment of opposing views, and treating interesting mechanisms as complete explanations. For example, one post conflates concern about democratic breakdown with unwillingness to accept electoral defeat; another bundles male economic difficulties under a label that risks doing explanatory work. The author notes honest caveats in Cowen's May 25, 2016 conjecture but concludes the strongest starting points are Democracy and the Democrats (October 22, 2022) and The Gaslighting of Parasite (June 25, 2020).
items.title: An Analysis of Weakly Reasoned MR Posts

items.summary: Harriet Dart won her first career WTA singles title, defeating Austrian Lilli Tagger 4-6 6-3 6-4 in the Guangzhou Open final on Sunday. The British player, ranked 115th and coached by former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli, overcame a sluggish start after being broken in the opening game. She steadied to hold for 5-3 in the deciding set, closing out the match after trading five consecutive breaks of serve.
items.title: Harriet Dart Wins First WTA Singles Title in Guangzhou

items.summary: For the 25th anniversary of Heidi Klum’s New York Halloween party on Saturday, 31 October, celebrities gathered in elaborate costumes. Klum headlined with a transformation into a giant severed hand featuring dangling ligaments and tendons, only her eyes and mouth visible, blood dripping from her mouth, accompanied by helpers in blood-stained hazmat suits. The idea came to her last year when she considered fitting her entire body inside a giant version of her left hand.
items.title: Heidi Klum Costume as Giant Severed Hand at Halloween Party

items.summary: Yuliia Mayfeld, 39, and her children returned to their home in Kherson after nearly five years away. They had fled the region amid fighting between Ukrainian and Russian forces, taking refuge in Odesa. Using a weeklong humanitarian truce brokered by First Lady Melania Trump, which was set to end Sunday evening, they passed through checkpoints manned by soldiers before arriving at their residence.
items.title: Ukrainian Family Returns Home Under Kherson Truce

items.summary: Cotality reports Australian median house prices have fallen $63,400 since March, the steepest pace in four decades. National values dropped 1.2 per cent in October and sit 6.7 per cent below their March peak. Cotality's Gerard Burg calls it a demand-led downturn as higher interest rates cut borrowing capacity. Home sales fell 23 per cent over three months, auction clearance sits under 50 per cent, and median time on market reached 39 days. Nicola Powell of Domain warns price cuts could reach 10 per cent. Recovery is expected only after rate signals shift in late 2027. Agents report weak buyer confidence amid tax changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax.
items.title: Australian home prices hit fastest 40-year decline

items.summary: A new McKinnon Index survey conducted with Roy Morgan in June and July found that more than 27 per cent of young men aged 18 to 24 say extreme measures, such as violence, can sometimes be justified to advance a cause. This compares with about one in ten across the whole population. The research surveyed more than 4,000 Australians on attitudes toward democracy and found support for democracy among young men fell to 54 per cent, while trust in politicians declined nationally. McKinnon chairman John Thwaites said those who justified violence remained a minority but were growing. University of Melbourne's Aaron Martin noted Australia sits between countries doing badly and well globally.
items.title: Survey Finds Rising Support for Extreme Measures Among Young Australian Men

items.summary: Largely peaceful Gen Z protests against rising living costs turned violent across several German cities on Saturday as rioters clashed with police and looted shops. Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt am Main and Cologne saw burning barricades, smashed windows and water cannon deployments; 27 officers were injured in Berlin while around 120 people were detained there. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed left-wing groups and troublemakers from a migrant background for the unrest.
items.title: Gen Z Protests Turn Violent Across Germany

items.summary: The Ministry of Finance announced on 31 October 2026 that the Centre released ₹1,09,019 crore as a second additional instalment of tax devolution during FY27. The payment is over and above regular monthly transfers, timed ahead of the festive season to help states accelerate capital expenditure and meet development and welfare spending needs. Uttar Pradesh received the largest share at ₹19,208 crore, followed by Bihar (₹10,845 crore) and Madhya Pradesh (₹8,010 crore). The release is attributed to the Ministry of Finance as a measure to support states before festive-season expenditure commitments. Tax devolution refers to transferring states' share of Union tax revenue to state governments.
items.title: Centre Releases Extra Tax Devolution Instalment to States

items.summary: FRANCE 24 recaps striking images from the past week, covering Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil's presidential polls, razor-sharp margins in Israel's general elections, and a deadly high-speed train collision in Spain.
items.title: FRANCE 24 Reviews Striking Images From a Busy Week

items.summary: The author recounts importing a $2,000 electric mini-truck from China and using it for over five years as an off-road work vehicle on their parents' 10-acre property in Florida. Initially doubted by skeptics who expected rapid failure or heavy rust, the truck has instead kept most systems working: windows, locks, headlights, backup camera, and air conditioning all function, with AC vents reaching about 55°F (12°C). Rust is limited to scratched areas near the tailgate and bed lip. The author's father praised it as an essential piece of equipment with negligible operating costs—charging a full battery runs just over a dollar—and said he'd expect another five or ten years of use. The truck remains non-street-legal, lacks safety features, has no odometer for mileage tracking, and its range suits only the property's needs.
items.title: A $2,000 Chinese electric truck survives five years on a Florida homestead

items.summary: An India Today crew was assaulted by an unidentified mob while covering civic elections in Pulivendula, Andhra Pradesh. The attackers damaged equipment to destroy footage of alleged stone pelting and booth capturing. A complaint has been registered at the police station. YSRCP chief Jagan Mohan Reddy blamed TDP for orchestrating attacks, while TDP countered with allegations of voter intimidation across multiple constituencies.
items.title: India Today Crew Assaulted in Pulivendula; Cyclone Murasu Approaches East Coast

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated 23 development projects worth ₹307.83 crore in Gujarat's Ekta Nagar on Saturday, per news agency PTI, and laid foundation stones for eight more initiatives worth ₹118.88 crore. The combined programme involves a total investment of ₹426.71 crore across tourist attractions, connectivity improvements and civic amenities around the Statue of Unity. Highlights include an IRCTC hotel costing ₹50 crore, the Ekta Cruise at ₹16 crore, travelators worth ₹28.22 crore and sewage treatment facilities valued at ₹45.53 crore. The Gujarat government aims to develop the area into a broader tourism hub beyond its landmark attraction.
items.title: Modi Inaugurates Tourism and Infrastructure Projects Near Statue of Unity

items.summary: An India Today crew covering civic elections in Pulivendula, Andhra Pradesh was assaulted by an unidentified mob. Reporters Abdul Basheer and Vijay said attackers snatched their camera, battery and memory card to destroy footage of alleged stone pelting and booth capturing near the Gandhi statue, police station and a school in Havilipuram. Accounts from the ground put the mob at 50 to 80 people. A complaint was lodged at Pulivendula police station after YSRCP chief Jagan Mohan Reddy staged a dharna blaming TDP for barring polling agents.
items.title: India Today Crew Attacked During Pulivendula Civic Poll Coverage

items.summary: The writer opens by quoting a view that gardening is an endless war with evil, its victory worth winning, before turning to Reginald Arkell’s 1950 novel of the garden. Published when Arkell was 78 and born in 1881, the book follows Herbert ‘Bert’ Pinnegar, whose life mirrors his author’s, from boyish helper under Mr Addis to head gardener at the Charteris estate. The story spans into the Second World War as machinery crowds out hand tending and gardens become vegetable patches; Mrs Charteris opens her grounds through the National Garden Scheme of 1927 while Bert resists strangers in his Eden. Arkell, who wrote a welcoming poem for the Scheme, contrasts with Bert’s disapproval. The reviewer calls it ‘a sweet, quick-witted novel about cherishing old friendships and tending to small joys of life’ (Modern Library).
items.title: A Reviewer Finds Comfort in Old Herbaceous

items.summary: Forest Service and park officials report that AI chatbots are increasingly steering outdoor visitors into trouble. On Mount Shasta in Northern California, three hikers relied on Google's Gemini before getting lost after summiting at 7:30 pm; another visitor camped near a No Camping sign because an AI told her she could, and a man used an AI-generated map showing features on the wrong side of a mountain. Grand Teton National Park Superintendent Chip Jenkins said AI use for travel information rose from zero to 26 percent over the past year. Nick Meyers noted it remains unclear whether this rise will increase rescues; his office averaged about a dozen annually in 2026, while Wyoming saw fewer calls than prior years. Experts warn chatbots can hallucinate and foster 'cognitive surrender,' urging people to verify against authoritative maps or talk to rangers.
items.title: AI Chatbots Lead Hikers Astray, Prompting Rescues

items.summary: Plant Heritage, a UK-based plant conservation charity, has awarded Chester Zoo's collection of Dracula orchids the status of National Plant Collection. The zoo looks after more than 75 of the 147 scientifically recognised species of these Andean cloud-forest orchids, making it one of the most significant collections of the genus and its sixth such recognition overall. According to Brie Langley, Assistant Team Manager at Chester Zoo's plant nursery, the flowers require conditions closely resembling their natural habitat. The award highlights conservation efforts amid threats from habitat loss, illegal extraction and mining in South America.
items.title: Chester Zoo Collection Recognised as National Plant Collection

items.summary: The CBI secured the extradition of Sourabh Chandrakar, alleged mastermind behind the ₹6,000-crore Mahadev online betting syndicate, from Oman. A specially deputed team escorted him back to India, where he will face the CBI Special Court in Raipur, an anonymous officer told Hindustan Times.
items.title: Mahadev Betting App Promoter Extradited From Oman

items.summary: Seven trekkers and one guide went missing after being stranded on the Kedartal trek in Uttarkashi district. The group of 13 people set out from Gangotri on October 27, with a planned return on October 29, but heavy snowfall and glaciers blocked their route. On Sunday, SDRF personnel conducted aerial reconnaissance over the area and found no clear signs of the missing individuals or their tents. One stranded trekker has sustained a head injury.
items.title: SDRF launches search for seven trekkers stranded in Uttarakhand’s Kedartal

items.summary: Hero MotoCorp launched the Hero Destini 110 Classique Edition scooter during the festival season. Priced at ₹76,400 ex-showroom Delhi, it adds two dual-tone colour options, a 3D classic badge and matching mirrors, seat and rim tape to the standard model. The company says no changes were made to the basic design or mechanical parts.
items.title: Hero Launches Destini 110 Classique Edition Scooter at ₹76,400

items.summary: The Civil Aviation Ministry said on Sunday that Digi Yatra trials for international passengers have started at seven airports - Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar. The facility is expected to roll out in 2027 after feedback from November to December this year is used. Trials are available to Indian nationals holding e-passports on select Air India and IndiGo flights, complementing rather than replacing existing travel processes while passengers continue mandatory checks.
items.title: Civil Aviation Ministry launches Digi Yatra trials for international flyers at seven airports

items.summary: UDP chief Metbah Lyngdoh resigned from the Conrad K Sangma-led Meghalaya Democratic Alliance government on October 31, citing that his party had been reduced to a single legislator after 11 of its 12 MLAs left. Eight defected to the BJP in September and three to the NPP earlier in October.
items.title: Meghalaya UDP Chief Resigns After Mass MLA Defections

items.summary: A federal judge in Miami dismissed Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch, ruling he failed to prove actual malice required by the 1964 New York Times Co. v. Sullivan standard. The case concerned a report about an Epstein birthday album letter allegedly bearing Trump's name.
items.title: Judge dismisses Trump's $10 billion lawsuit over Epstein letter story

items.summary: OPEC+ members kept their oil production targets steady for December at an online meeting on Sunday, Nov 1, matching expectations that no policy change would come until next year. The group cites ongoing export disruptions from the US-Iran war as it struggles to reach its goals. Most Gulf producers still pump well below target levels.
items.title: OPEC+ Holds December Output Targets Amid Iran War Disruptions

items.summary: Matt Barreto, a UCLA political science professor and BSP Research co-founder who advised Democratic campaigns in 2016, 2020 and 2024, says his latest polling points to Latino voters returning to the party after backing Donald Trump. He warns this reflects rejection of Trump rather than growing support for Democrats, calling it one data point rather than a trend. Barreto attributes turnout to economic frustration over prices, tariffs and health care costs, plus anger at immigration policy. Polls show Democrats on pace to win back the House by about seven points; he calls that almost certain but sees the Senate as more open.
items.title: Barreto frames Latino midterm shift as a repudiation of Trump, not a trend

items.summary: Algeria announced plans to deploy army units into neighbouring Niger, marking a departure from its long-standing reluctance to send forces abroad. On 25 October 2026, both chambers of Algeria's parliament approved the deployment, and President Abdelmadjid Tebboune authorised it on 26 October 2026, saying it would protect shared energy and economic interests. The two countries share a 951km border. Analysts note that securing oil or gas facilities does not automatically secure surrounding areas, raising concerns the mission could expand beyond its stated scope. Details such as troop numbers, deployment location and rules of engagement remain unconfirmed.
items.title: Algeria's First Troop Deployment to Niger in Decades Raises Strategic Questions

items.summary: Lauren Johnston, a specialist in China trade with Africa, has published China, Africa and the Market for Donkeys. She says demand for donkey hides grew over 15 years, driven almost exclusively by China’s use of ejiao, a gelatin-based tonic consumed by tens of millions of women. One hide can fetch over US$400 in China. The trade draws mainly on Africa, which holds about two-thirds of the world’s donkeys. Johnston cites the Donkey Sanctuary as estimating that China imports more than three million hides annually, 25%-35% stolen. A February 2024 African Union Summit agreed a moratorium; Johnston notes implementation remains imperfect and progress is far from enough to save the animal.
items.title: New Book Traces China's Donkey Hide Trade and Its Impact on Africa

items.summary: Solar Mounts LLC, a Michigan-based solar mounting company represented by Terence Parker, frames the U.S. Department of Energy’s October 12, 2026 emergency order directing PJM Interconnection to use additional generating resources as a warning sign for its state and region. The author notes the order permits designated plants to exceed operating limits and allows backup generators at large facilities during emergencies, but cautions that blackouts are not inevitable. Citing PJM capacity auction prices of $329.17 per megawatt-day for 2026–2027 and $333.44 for 2027–2028, the piece argues for faster deployment of solar, wind, batteries, and nuclear rather than relying on temporary fossil-fuel measures. It also addresses agrivoltaics in Calhoun County and data center power demands as part of its broader call to build capacity before the next crisis.
items.title: Michigan Company Urges Power Buildout After DOE Emergency Order

items.summary: With Alaska pollock catches shrinking and fuel costs high, Japan’s processed fish product-makers face rising surimi prices ahead of winter demand. A Japanese trading house is working with a Vietnamese seafood company to use farmed Vietnam pangasius catfish instead. “More than 1.6 million tons of pangasius are produced annually in Vietnam,” said a trading house official, noting the paste’s quality and future supply potential.
items.title: Vietnam pangasius eyed as surimi alternative

items.summary: Some migrants have found shelter at an upgraded reception camp near Nicosia, where The Associated Press was granted access. Menemah, a 24-year-old lesbian rejected by her family in Cameroon, said she hopes another EU country may take up her asylum case because Cyprus may not. She is among 343 migrants currently residing at the center, including 72 unaccompanied minors.
items.title: Migrants Find Shelter in Cyprus as EU Slows Admissions

items.summary: On Sunday at the Manama Dialogue 2026, Yemen's Foreign Minister Afrah al-Zouba met with the UK's Middle East and North Africa Minister Stephen Doughty. According to a statement by Yemen's Foreign Ministry, they discussed bilateral ties and efforts to counter the Houthis, plus the worsening humanitarian situation in Taiz under a Houthi-imposed siege. Doughty reaffirmed continued UK support for Yemen's internationally recognised government.
items.title: Yemeni and UK Ministers Discuss Ties, Houthi Counter-Efforts

items.summary: The Youth Olympic Games opened Saturday in Diamniadio, near Dakar, marking the first Olympic event held on the African continent as the region seeks a larger role in international sport. Tens of thousands attended the ceremony at the Diamniadio Olympic Stadium, where drummers and dancers performed under the motto “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates.” Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye declared it open. About 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 will compete through Nov. 13 across 153 medal events in 25 sports. The first refugee team at a Youth Olympics fields six athletes from Kenya and Uganda.
items.title: Youth Olympic Games Open in Senegal

items.summary: At a rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, Rahul Gandhi said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be removed and jailed, calling the 2024 Lok Sabha polls illegal. He alleged votes were stolen through electronic voting machines and voter-list tampering after about 15 per cent of voters were dropped in 2024. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Centre and state governments came to power by vote theft and that democracy survives only if Modi leaves office. BJP leaders countered, calling the Special Intensive Revision a political controversy.
items.title: Congress Leaders Denounce EVMs and Demand CEC's Removal

items.summary: On Sunday, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw visited BEML's Bengaluru facility manufacturing India's first bullet train and inspected its progress. Speaking to ANI, he said the progress is excellent and that major components are being produced, integrated and tested with emphasis on quality. Testing occurs at loads of 1,500 kilonewtons according to international standards. Separately, PM Narendra Modi approved the Northern Bullet Train Corridor linking Delhi and Varanasi.
items.title: Railway Minister shows progress at India's first bullet train plant

items.summary: Analysts expect ITC's cigarette volumes to decline around 8% year-on-year, while operating profit from the business could fall as much as 29%, as higher taxes and insufficient price increases weigh on margins. Nuvama Equities projects a 3% revenue decline hurt by weakness in cigarettes and subdued agriculture, partially offset by FMCG growth, alongside a 20% EBITDA drop with margin contracting to around 28.5%. JM Financial and Motilal Oswal also flag cigarette earnings pressure while expecting healthy non-cigarette growth. The company's pricing strategy and volume stabilization pace will be key for investors in the upcoming results.
items.title: ITC Q2 Profit Seen Falling Nearly 30% as Cigarette Tax Hikes Bite

items.summary: Actress Susan Sarandon sits for an interview with the Spanish outlet EL PAÍS’ fashion supplement Smoda just days before turning 80. The conversation covers her career, family and decades of activism. She discusses playing foster mothers in films such as The Accompanist and Dead Man Walking, which earned her an Academy Award nomination. Sarandon describes how becoming a mother shaped her flexible approach to scheduling work around her children. On her long history of protest — including arrests at the United Nations over Benjamin Netanyahu’s address, on Lesbos for migrants, and in 2018 against child separation at the U.S.-Mexico border — she says she is not a victim but wants people talking about what happens there. When asked whether activism has cost her work, she replies it happened before but never badly. She also addresses being called a communist, saying she considers herself an independent patriot who votes in general elections.
items.title: Susan Sarandon Reflects on Activism, Acting and Age in EL PAÍS Interview

items.summary: A US judge dismissed President Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.4bn) defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal and its parent company Dow Jones, ruling the case was 'grasping at straws' and violated the First Amendment. Judge Darrin Gayles threw out the lawsuit with prejudice after reporting on a letter allegedly written by Trump for Jeffrey Epstein's 2003 birthday book.
items.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein book report

items.summary: A California federal judge ordered the Department of Justice to stop demanding that local and state election officials set aside ballots it alleges may come from non-citizens, ruling days before the midterms. Judge Trina Thompson said the demands could interfere with elections and disenfranchise lawful voters. Trump criticised the decision while civil rights groups had filed the complaint.
items.title: Federal judge bars Trump administration from threatening election officials

items.summary: Airbnb has updated its host guidelines so that, from bookings made globally on 20 November, hosts can no longer require guests to perform tasks usually done by cleaners, such as washing dishes or stripping beds. The change follows complaints about lengthy checkouts layered on top of cleaning fees. Host Lisa Clewes says the rules could force extra cleanings and higher costs; guest Jessica Newhook welcomed them after being asked to prepare a property for 11 guests despite paying $250 (£187). Cleaner Krissi Foskett said professional cleaning is a cost of business, while host Anthony Marsh cut his listings from five to two. Data provider AirROI reports that 63.2% of Airbnb listings charge an average £55 cleaning fee. Some hosts, including Matt Prosz and Laura Lewis, see the update as improving guest experience or reducing platform dependence.
items.title: Airbnb's new checkout rules split hosts and guests over washing up

items.summary: A Reader's Digest roundup lists several November 2026 holidays and observances to add to a calendar. It frames the month as offering traditions, charitable causes and lighter food-themed days worth celebrating. The article presents National Adoption Month, World Vegan Day on November 1, National Cappuccino Day on November 8, Veterans Day on November 11, World Kindness Day on November 13, and National Philanthropy Day on November 15 as starting points for discovering new traditions or marking important dates. Each entry describes what the observance encourages rather than stating facts about it independently.
items.title: Reader's Digest rounds up November 2026 holidays and observances

items.summary: Samuel King, a PhD student in the Stanford University lab behind the work, watched petri dishes overnight when clear spots began spreading across bacteria. A virus his team had designed on a computer was alive and killing. Lab leader Brian Hie recalled that when colleagues saw the results, the room spontaneously burst into applause.
items.title: Human scientists, not AI, still control biosecurity fate

items.summary: On 1 November, Rahul Gandhi led the INDIA bloc’s ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of electoral misconduct. He alleged large-scale voter deletions affecting 13.5 crore voters after the 2024 elections, calling it treason rather than ordinary theft. Reporting from The Hindu, Hindustan Times, and Financial Express documented his claims.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Warns Modi Over Alleged Vote Manipulation at Delhi Rally

items.summary: India's leading automakers reported strong October 2026 domestic sales, with festive demand driving record monthly volumes. Maruti Suzuki India posted its highest-ever monthly figure of 2,16,789 units, up 20% year-on-year. Mahindra & Mahindra recorded its best monthly SUV total of 73,338 units, up 2%, while Hyundai Motor India reached record sales of 62,799 units, a gain of 16.7%. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles also posted robust growth.
items.title: Indian carmakers hit record October domestic sales on festive demand

items.summary: OpenAI announced it is rolling out ChatGPT Work capabilities into regular Chat, combining usage allowances across the two services. The combined experience will be tested with a small group of users before wider rollout. Separately, OpenAI doubled Work and Codex allowances for its Pro 100, Pro 200, and Pro 500 subscriptions, effective October 29.
items.title: OpenAI Expands ChatGPT Work Features and Doubles Pro Usage Limits

items.summary: Actor Ranbir Kapoor, playing Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana adaptation, compared the mythical Pushpaka Vimana to Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster. During a Star Talks interview with co-stars Yash, Ravie Dubey and Rakul Preet Singh, he said India had flying cars 5,000 years ago, while Musk recently demonstrated his vehicle at SpaceX in Texas on October 15.
items.title: Ranbir Kapoor Compares Ancient Flying Car To Musk Roadster

items.summary: UOL Group and CapitaLand Development said Thomson Reserve sold 1,143 of 1,268 units – about 90% – at an average price of $2,900 per sq ft during the launch weekend. Developers described demand as strong across unit types near Upper Thomson MRT station. PropNex CEO Kelvin Fong said it was the most units sold over a launch weekend in 2026, surpassing Tengah Garden Residences’ 853 units. Nicholas Mak of Mogul.sg noted the result reversed declining take-up rates at residential launches.
items.title: Thomson Reserve sells most of its units over a launch weekend in Singapore

items.summary: OpenAI said on Friday it is tightening limits on weapons-related information that ChatGPT provides to teens, even when a question appears harmless, as part of new safeguards aimed at preventing real-world violence. The company will restrict practical details on misusable weapons and security systems, automatically end chats where users appear fixated on violence, strengthen its age-prediction system for those it estimates are under 18 into the teen experience, limit detail on past mass attacks, pause accounts after repeated violent discussions, and notify parents if a teen's account is paused.
items.title: OpenAI Tightens ChatGPT Weapons Info for Teens

items.summary: DeepSeek released a prototype open-source coding agent called Super-Agent that monitors developer group chats and suggests solutions without being summoned. The DeepSeek Harness team said it aims to minimize human attention while maximizing value. It targets Claude Code from Anthropic amid growing rivalry between Chinese firms and US labs over AI tools.
items.title: DeepSeek Launches Autonomous Coding Agent Super-Agent to Challenge Anthropic, OpenAI

items.summary: In a Forum piece, George Goh argues that Singapore's one-bedroom condominium market shows a mismatch: units attract tenants but are hard to sell. He highlights the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) at 60% as prohibitive for foreign buyers and asks whether the Government could offer a targeted concession restricted to owner-occupied units below a floor area, with holding-period conditions.
items.title: Forum Calls for ABSD Concession on Foreign Buyers of One-Bedroom Homes

items.summary: Ryan Joshua Mahindapala, an educator writing under the initials K.B., submitted a letter urging the National Library Board (NLB) to review its ReadSG Challenge and consider safeguards. He expressed concern that participants can log reading time without verification, which could allow people to report reading hours for rewards without actually reading. He suggested measures such as simple comprehension questions or integration with digital platforms.
items.title: Educator urges NLB to add safeguards to ReadSG Challenge

items.summary: The BJP accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday of attempting to sideline his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, alleging she was denied a speaking opportunity at the INDIA bloc rally in Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. National spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari claimed growing divisions within Congress and that Rahul had suppressed her during both the event and Saturday's mock parliament exercise.
items.title: BJP Accuses Rahul Gandhi of Sidelining Sister at Rally

items.summary: Union minister H. D. Kumaraswamy challenged Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh over a sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah, saying the phone used was bought in New Delhi and handed to his official residence. Kumaraswamy promised complete details on Monday but declined immediate answers about the investigation's stage or whose position the commissioner is protecting.
items.title: Kumaraswamy Defies Police Over Sting Investigation Details

items.summary: The SumSum presents an abstract mathematics challenge dated November 2026, asking solvers to compute the 'SumSum' of sequences built by repeatedly removing first elements and forming partial sums. It gives one worked example yielding 16,796 for a ten-element input, then requests answers modulo specific values, with a bonus task offering additional credit.
items.title: SumSum puzzle challenges readers with a sequence problem

items.summary: In a CGTN First Voice column, the writer argues that US midterm election campaigns and outside groups are spending large sums to tell Americans that everyday life has become unaffordable. The piece notes the message is about affordability but observes that the delivery remains costly, suggesting the spending itself may undermine the point being made.
items.title: CGTN Column Frames Midterm Spending as Priciest Message Yet

items.summary: When Chinese President Xi Jinping and Swiss President Guy Parmelin signed a protocol upgrading the two countries' free trade agreement on October 30, commentators described it as an event of multifold significance. The original deal dates to 2013, when Switzerland became among the first Western nations to recognize China's People's Republic. Bilateral goods trade in 2025 reached around CHF 33.5 billion ($40.66 billion). Once the upgrade takes effect, products subject to zero tariff will account for more than 99% of bilateral trade value, up from 53.6% under the original agreement. Alexandr Svetlicinii, a CGTN commentator, frames it as a reference point for future China-EU economic relations amid heightened trade tensions. The article notes Swiss company views but states opinions are its own.
items.title: Switzerland-China FTA Upgrade Signals Reference for China-EU Trade

items.summary: Hollywood director Michael Mann was taken to a hospital after an apparently accidental shooting at The Range LA in Los Angeles, according to the Associated Press and TMZ. At 83, he reportedly shot himself in the leg while holstering his weapon, sustaining what his representative called a superficial injury.
items.title: Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidental Gun Discharge

items.summary:
French officials have opened an investigation into the attempted murder of a police officer after petrol bombs were thrown at officers during Saturday-night protests across France. The prosecutor’s office in Paris said incendiary devices were thrown at about 15 gendarmes and police, opening a case for “attempted murder of persons vested with public authority.” Germany’s interior minister Alexander Dobrindt called for harsh penalties, singling out violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from the migrant community. In Frankfurt, looters damaged shops and injured more than 100 officers; Hesse’s Roman Poseck said police faced “between 1,000 and 1,500 violent troublemakers.” The Gen Z regelt campaign distanced itself from all violence.

visual:null
items.title: France Opens Attempted-Murder Probe After Petrol Bomb Thrown at Police

items.summary: Four crew members of NASA's simulated Mars mission, the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA), emerged after 378 days in isolation at Johnson Space Center in Houston. The analog aimed to prepare astronauts for future long-duration space travel.
items.title: NASA Mars Mission Crew Emerges After Nearly a Year in Isolation

items.summary: The post is titled “Sunday assorted links” and lists several items, including a song cycle by Jakob Davidsen called The Individual and the Entire Tissue. It notes that piece as good, then reports that an “endless cruise has ended,” alongside other brief cultural and research topics.
items.title: Sunday assorted links opens with a music review and a culture note.

items.summary: Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui won the New York City Marathon Sunday, finishing in two hours, 24 minutes and 36 seconds while running alone.
