She is defending champion after holding off Hellen Obiri last year. Sweden's Andreas Almgren took his debut men's title with a time of 2:06:01, edging Italian Yemaneberhan Crippa by 13 seconds. Chepkirui said the final mile was tricky and she had to push up to the line; Almgren added he might start crying over such a good debut.
items.title: Chepkirui Reclaims New York Marathon Title in Debut Win for Almgren

items.summary: India's two-wheeler retail market rose nearly 29 per cent in October, though the festive boom masked uneven recovery as five major makers grew slower than average. Hero MotoCorp and Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India supplied about two-thirds of extra registrations, lifting their combined share to 53.26 per cent from 50.33 per cent. BusinessLine's calculations put total October registrations at 23,20,139 units, up 28.7 per cent month-on-month. Honda narrowed Hero's calendar-year lead sharply, but Hero stays overall leader on electric sales. Analyst Aveek Chattopadhyay said the strength reflected pent-up demand, yet November could soften with fewer working days and weak rural purchasing power.
items.title: Hero and Honda Drive October Two-Wheeler Sales Surge

items.summary: Amba told PTI that 15 of the 18 vehicles in JLR's newly unveiled Range Rover SV Sawai Collection were already pre-booked, reflecting a premium India's luxury buyers are paying. The three-edition collection is priced around Rs 5 crore and marks growth from 12 to 18 units. Amba said 'India has truly arrived.' JLR also plans electric Range Rovers in calendar year 2027.
items.title: JLR's Range Rover Sawai Collection Sees Strong Pre-Bookings Amid Luxury Demand

items.summary: Speaking to ANI, Ilahi, Iran's Supreme Leader's representative, said the country wants peace but will defend itself with its lives and blood if attacked. He dismissed expectations that Iran would hand over oil or minerals as a dream that will never come true. Remarks followed Trump's call with Netanyahu amid Washington weighing renewed military action against Iran.
items.title: Iran Vows It Will Not Surrender If US Attacks

items.summary: Pitjantjatjara artist Sally Scales, chair of the National Gallery of Australia's First Nations advisory group, says artificial intelligence is taking First Nations art and turning it into low-quality goods sold online. She calls it a theft of cultural knowledge that undermines artists' agency and authenticity. The article notes AI has been trained without compensation on works by Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave, despite government vows to protect creatives from copyright theft. Experts warn the risks are especially acute for Indigenous cultural property. Kathy Bowrey of UNSW Law says one in five creators already faces infringement problems that worsen with First Nations artists.
items.title: Artist Says AI Steals Indigenous Art Into Temu Slop

items.summary: Heidi Klum unveiled an elaborate Halloween party costume in New York, appearing as a gigantic, bloody enlarged copy of her left hand. According to Vogue, body scans were used to create it. Details such as her engagement and wedding rings and the tattoo with Tom Kaulitz's name were included. Special effects make-up artist Mike Marino produced it.
items.title: Heidi Klum's Halloween costume becomes a giant bloody replica of her own hand

items.summary: Americans gained an extra hour of sleep on Sunday, November 1, as daylight saving time ended for 2026. Clocks were turned back by one hour at 2 am local time across most parts of the United States. The practice was first introduced in 1918 during World War I and later standardized through Congress's Uniform Time Act in 1966, with a schedule extended under a 2005 law taking effect in 2007. Lawmakers continue debating permanent time; earlier in 2026 the Sunshine Protection Act passed the House of Representatives and was sent to the Senate for consideration. President Donald Trump has backed the proposal.
items.title: US ends daylight saving time for 2026 amid debate over permanent clocks

items.summary: Russian state media reported that the Federal Security Service detained a minor Russian citizen after he posted images on TikTok resembling tactical gear near the Tsaritsyno Museum-Reserve. The U.S. embassy issued an alert warning of a credible threat of a mass casualty event and advised people to avoid crowds, while coordinating with Russian authorities.
items.title: Russia arrests minor after US embassy warns of 'credible threat of a mass casualty event'

items.summary: Bangladesh established a six-member wage board to review pay in its garment industry after violent protests over low wages forced more than 500 factories to suspend operations. According to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, unrest has shut down 529 factories, leaving nearly 987,190 workers without work. Workers demand a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (around $245), more than double the existing rate of 12,500 taka. The government urged employees to return and warned that prolonged closures could delay export shipments. Labour minister Ariful Haque Choudhury said the panel will recommend revised pay rates after discussions with workers and employers.
items.title: Bangladesh Forms Wage Board Amid Garment Worker Protests

items.summary: The mutilated bodies of two Kuki men, T Chongloi and Paoginlal Hangsing, went missing from Taphou Kuki village on October 29. Police recovered them from a banana farm during a joint search involving multiple forces but have not identified those responsible. Protesters allege Naga militants abducted and killed them, sparking clashes with security forces in Kangpokpi. The discovery followed three more community deaths amid ongoing ethnic violence since February.
items.title: Kuki men found dead in gunny bags triggers Manipur protests

items.summary: A recent look at social media revealed roughly half of one feed filled with machine-generated content, prompting reflection on trust in information. The piece highlights the challenge facing publishers as artificial intelligence produces increasingly plausible fake papers, described by Eliza Strickland as effortless generation that bypasses review systems. It also examines Wikipedia's volunteer efforts to keep its content human-written and warns that uncertainty about what is real may ultimately undermine trust in institutions.
items.title: Editors Fight Back Against AI-Generated Slop in Publishing and Wikipedia

items.summary: Delhi Police's Special Cell arrested three people for allegedly writing pro-Khalistan slogans targeting singer Diljit Dosanjh. The graffiti, discovered on October 29 and 30 respectively, appeared near Gate No 1 of Jahangirpuri Metro station (Yellow Line) and on the inner wall of a staircase at Shastri Nagar Metro station (Red Line). Police suspect a conspiracy linked to Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), with one associate coordinating operations after receiving designs and money from an SFJ member. The slogans read,
items.title: Three Arrested Over Pro-Khalistan Graffiti Targeting Diljit Dosanjh at Delhi Metro Stations

items.summary: Emma Reynolds, chief secretary to the treasury, told GB News that employers are companies rather than working people during a Sunday interview. Conservative politicians condemned the remark as patronising and out of touch with small-business owners who employ apprentices and weekend workers. The exchange revived scrutiny of Labour's 2024 pledge not to raise taxes on working people after former chancellor Rachel Reeves increased employers' national insurance from 13.5% to 15%, reducing its threshold from £9,100 to £5,000 in October 2024. A Treasury spokesperson defended the government's position as consistent with manifesto commitments.
items.title: Labour minister draws fire over employers not being 'working people'

items.summary: This article on The Conversation argues that Jonathan Swift's experience as a member of Ireland's Protestant elite shaped the satire in his 1726 novel, first published October 28. It notes the group saw itself as bringing order to Ireland while facing being treated as inferior themselves. A quoted contemporary, William Molyneux, observed that oppression would make them 'turn Irish.' The piece links Swift's dual perspective across Gulliver's Travels and works like his 1729 essay A Modest Proposal to the folly of allegiance to a power that oppresses him, calling the book relevant 300 years after publication. It first appeared on The Conversation.
items.title: Swift's Irish Identity Shaped Gulliver's Travels

items.summary: The European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, deepening Poland's constitutional crisis on Saturday. The standoff comes ahead of next year's parliamentary election, with polls suggesting a close race between Tusk's coalition and the nationalist right.
items.title: Poland's Constitutional Crisis Deepens Over Judge Appointments Ahead of Election

items.summary: John Smedley, a heritage knitwear maker with the world's oldest continuously operating factory, is investing £4m to update machinery and expand its range. The company faces difficult market conditions: sales fell 5% to £16.8m for the year ending 31 March 2025, as a weak yen hurt Japan trade, which accounts for half of international business. The group reported a £720,000 pre-tax loss compared with a £270,000 profit previously. Managing director Jess McGuire-Dudley says the firm is in a turnaround and that recent efforts have driven its first UK sales growth in over five years. Family owners remain committed to British manufacturing despite higher costs.
items.title: John Smedley Invests in Machinery Amid Tough Luxury Market

items.summary: Tim Seifert fell seven runs short of his first international hundred after scoring 93 off 50 balls in the fifth and final T20I, losing out when a Nitish Kumar Reddy delivery hit him onto the stumps. New Zealand won by seven wickets to clinch the series 3-2 over India at Seddon Park. Seifert joked that his century was still 'on my back' with heavier shoulders after the miss. Teammate Glenn Phillips led the series with 341 runs, breaking Phil Salt's record of 331 for most runs in a bilateral T20I series and becoming one of only three batters to post four or more half-centuries. Seifert praised Phillips' patient approach as he focused on winning rather than chasing the personal milestone.
items.title: Seifert misses maiden century as New Zealand beat India

items.summary: Labour is less likely to meet its manifesto pledge to equalise the minimum wage for younger workers before the next election, after chancellor John Healey failed in a Sunday BBC interview to specify when the rise would occur. The budget raised adult and under-20 rates but offered no path toward closing the gap. Healey denied breaking the commitment while acknowledging trade-offs between jobs and wages.
items.title: Labour's under-20 minimum wage equalisation pledge faces doubt after budget omits timeline

items.summary: A 21-year-old man, Hemanth alias Dummu, accused of attacking a 15-year-old Class 10 student with a chainsaw at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu's Anantapur district on Saturday morning around 10.30am, was shot at by police Sunday night while allegedly trying to escape custody, officials said. He hurled stones during transport for a crime-scene reconstruction before police fired six rounds, leaving him seriously injured and transferred to Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru with critical condition. Education minister Nara Lokesh called the next 48 hours crucial and appealed for prayers for her recovery.
items.title: Andhra Suspect Shot At While Escaping Custody After Chainsaw Attack

items.summary: Before Diwali, gold fell about 22% and silver more than 55% from record highs. On October 30, MCX December gold futures traded at Rs 1,41,792 per 10 grams after dropping 0.56%, while December silver reached Rs 1,86,745 per kilo down 1.43%. Rising US inflation and lower rate-cut expectations are pressuring prices. Experts from Giottus.com's Vikram Subburaj and Enrich Money's Ponmudi R cite these factors and outline support levels, advising caution before buying.
items.title: Gold and silver prices fall sharply before Diwali, experts weigh in on buying timing

items.summary: A new 2027 Chevrolet Silverado police pursuit vehicle was shown at the Orange County Convention Center, fitted with a 402 hp version of the venerable 5.7 small-block Chevy V8 sending 428 lb-ft of torque through a 10-speed automatic transmission. The author notes that while an electric Silverado offers more than 750 hp in WOW mode and 775 lb-ft of torque at 0 rpm, police departments may still favor the gas-powered model.
items.title: Chevy Police Silverado Stays Gas-Powered Despite Electric Rival

items.summary: Tensions flared in Kangpokpi district, Manipur after the recovered bodies of two missing Kuki men who had reportedly been abducted on October 28. The deceased were identified as Paoginlal Hangshing and Tinginlun Chongloi. Their recovery triggered protests; at least three protesters were injured when demonstrators clashed with security forces. The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) refused to accept the bodies until its five demands, including safe release of the men, are met.
items.title: Kuki men's bodies trigger clashes in Manipur

items.summary: More than 4,000 residents were displaced on Sunday after Assam’s Dhubri district demolished the homes of over 640 Bengali Muslim families during an eviction drive, officials told Scroll. The demolition covered 650 bighas of government land in Alamganj Part-IX village, while notices had been served for 800 bighas; court cases halted work on the remaining 150 bighas. District Commissioner Dibakar Nath said residents settled there over five to ten years and that most hold land elsewhere, a claim disputed by resident Ali Chand Fakir, who cited touzi receipts from 1972 to 2016.
items.title: Assam Evicts Over 4,000 Residents After Demolishing Hundreds of Muslim Homes in Dhubri

items.summary: Yunna Kinereish, a 22-year-old Kazakh German in Astana, keeps her people's history alive through theater and film. She is one of 223,000 Kazakh Germans today, descendants of hundreds of thousands deported by Josef Stalin after Nazi Germany invaded the Soviet Union in 1941. More than a million were deported; at least 200,000 died from expulsion, hunger and forced labor. Kinereish's film covers German women imprisoned in ALZhIR, where 18,000 passed through between 1931 and 1959, including 167 ethnic Germans. Anthropologist Katherine M. Erdman notes that many Kazakhs show apathy toward this history, even as memorials like the Karlag complex—where about 10,000 prisoners died—are rarely visited.
items.title: Kazakh Germans Keep Soviet Deportation Legacy Alive

items.summary: French prosecutors opened an attempted murder investigation into rioters who threw a molotov cocktail at police during violent protests in Paris on Saturday. An officer suffered second-degree burns, and the prosecutor's office said explosive devices were thrown at around fifteen gendarmes as well as police officers. Investigators are working to identify those responsible, with no suspects in custody. The unrest followed hundreds of thousands of demonstrations over education and living costs, though shop damage was lower than previous weekends.
items.title: French Prosecutors Open Attempted Murder Probe After Rioters Throw Petrol Bomb at Police

items.summary: Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha called the Court of Arbitration for Sport decision allowing Russian ice hockey teams to return to world championships 'unacceptable.' He argued that letting Russia back while its attacks on Ukrainian cities continue would give Moscow international legitimacy it seeks, demanding there be no business as usual. The CAS overturned a ban Friday after an appeal by the Russian Ice Hockey Federation against the International Ice Hockey Federation.
items.title: Ukraine Rejects Return of Russian Ice Hockey Teams

items.summary: The largest wind farm in U.S. history, the SunZia project near Albuquerque, began operating this June with over 900 turbines connected to a 550-mile transmission line now powering more than 1 million homes as far as California (s3). Developed by Pattern Energy after taking over from Southwestern Power Group and securing $11 billion in financing (s46), it took roughly 17 years without breaking ground, hindered by permitting delays and high costs. The project's completion is framed as a model for future clean-energy megaprojects amid rising national electricity demand.
items.title: New Mexico's SunZia Wind Farm Finally Completed After Decades of Delays

items.summary: Experts warn that advances in AI and biotechnology could enable the development of biological weapons, a scenario security services now monitor closely. In October 2026, Ken McCallum, head of MI5, warned that artificial intelligence may increase risks from existing or new biological weapons, including those from non-state actors. A September 2026 report by Anthropic said it had identified and blocked numerous attempts to use its Claude assistant for possible weapon research, including gain-of-function studies and avian influenza variants potentially most transmissible to mammals. The article notes that distinguishing legitimate science from misuse remains a central challenge in controlling modern biotechnologies.
items.title: AI and biotechnology raise fears of biological weapons misuse

items.summary: Around a hundred people gathered Saturday in Sandton for South Africa's Pride parade, described as one of Africa's largest annual inclusivity celebrations. Participants waved rainbow flags and wore colorful costumes, some arriving from Asia and beyond. Patrick Smit-Stachowski explained his presence: 'As we've seen in countries like America, they are just taking away all the rights from transgender folks.' The article notes South Africa legalized same-sex marriage in 2006.
items.title: Hundreds Celebrate LGBTQ+ Pride in Johannesburg's Sandton District

items.summary: As host of COP29, Azerbaijan announced an ambitious climate target and urged other governments to follow suit. In the first nine months of 2026, renewables supplied about 20% of electricity production, up from roughly 13.4% in all of 2025, while total output reached approximately 21.2 billion kilowatt-hours versus 28.7 billion for the full year prior. The government plans to raise renewable share of installed capacity to about 33.3% by 2027 and aims for roughly 8 GW of new generation by 2032, with several solar and wind projects already online or under construction. Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov said renewables auctions are expected in 2028, and the country is also exploring nuclear development to diversify its energy mix.
items.title: Azerbaijan Accelerates Renewable Energy Expansion Amid COP29 Leadership

items.summary: In Sri Lanka, where roughly 70 per cent of the population is Buddhist and Buddhism enjoys state patronage, senior monks have long held privileged status. The dispute centered on Galagoda Atte Gnanasara, whose presidential pardon from 2019 was revoked by the Supreme Court in September this year, sending him back to prison for a further 63 months after he appeared without his robes. This sparked protests and marches of dozens of monks toward Colombo, some covering about 120 km. After staging a sit-in at Vihara Mahadevi Park involving curses critics called sacrilegious, the monks announced a temporary truce and withdrew. Commentators said ordinary Buddhists largely ignored them, reflecting limits on monk power. The Department of Buddhist Affairs noted more than 40,000 registered monks across some 12,000 temples.
items.title: Sri Lanka Buddhist Monks Retreat After Failed Protest Against Marxist Government

items.summary: Mo Ibrahim, head of the Mo Ibrahim Foundation and an 80-year-old Sudanese-British billionaire, told AFP that democracy and rights are declining across Africa as leaders follow strongman trends worldwide. The foundation's latest report finds broad progress on economic opportunity and human development over a decade but steep declines in security, human rights and public participation amid coups and wars. Ibrahim cited elections in Tanzania and Uganda, blamed global democratic decline from the United States to Europe and Russia, and called Washington's termination of USAID 'brutal'.
items.title: Mo Ibrahim Warns Africa's Democracy Is Declining Amid Global Rise of Strongmen

items.summary: The Rugby League World Cup semi-final between Tonga and Samoa ended 20-18 in favour of Tonga, with the result decided only in the final minute. The match drew the highest crowd at Parramatta Stadium and is seen as establishing a recurring Samoa-Tonga rivalry that could rival State of Origin for the new century. Both teams will meet again next week, with a possible World Cup final rematch still on the table despite both sides being likely outsiders.
items.title: Tonga and Samoa clash sets up State of Origin-style rivalry for new century

items.summary: State Election Commission Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said polling for 100 urban local bodies across Andhra Pradesh was mostly peaceful on Sunday. Around 40 incidents were reported and 275 FIRs registered, Inspector General of Police Rajakumari added. Preliminary voter turnout reached 48.03 percent by 3 pm, with the final figure to be announced Monday.
items.title: Andhra urban polls largely peaceful amid 275 FIRs, Election Commissioner says

items.summary: Hackers targeted a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-97229, in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20–21. The team rebuilt its GitLab server and reset all passwords because it could not rule out successful compromise due to missing logs. Although no tampering was found up to October 27, the attackers downloaded the container image, suggesting a possible supply-chain attack.
items.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack

items.summary: OPEC+ members kept their December production targets unchanged on Sunday, confirming that no policy changes are expected until next year. The seven core members decided in an online meeting amid ongoing export disruptions from the Iran war. Analyst Jorge Leon of Rystad called today's decision easy and pointed to November 29 as the harder test when OPEC+ decides its 2027 production framework, warning it faces huge uncertainty over the US-Iran war and recovery through the Strait of Hormuz.
items.title: OPEC+ Holds December Output Targets Steady as 2027 Review Looms

items.summary: A day after a helicopter crash in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) directed operators conducting Char Dham charter services to fly with two pilots from November 2 and obtain prior destination and enroute clearances for every flight sector. Operators threatened to suspend services from Monday, citing financial unviability due to increased costs.
items.title: 'Two pilots mandatory': DGCA tightens rules for Char Dham helicopter operators after crash

items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge became a social media meme after his remarks at the INDIA bloc's November 1, 2026 rally in Delhi went viral. Several clips show him telling people to stay quiet or face an hour-long speech, prompting users to joke about whether it was a rally or comedy show and calling it a 'weapon of mass boredom.' The rally protested electoral roll irregularities.
items.title: Congress president Kharge mocked after Ramlila Maidan rally remark

items.summary: Analysts note that upcoming U.S. midterms, spanning states from Alaska to Maine, could carry worldwide implications next week as midterm voting may weaken a president who has aggressively influenced global affairs. Polls suggest the Republican Party might lose control of at least one congressional chamber, which conventional analysis would frame as diminishing an 80-year-old leader's leverage over trade tariffs and military action. However, observers caution that Trump could instead treat domestic electoral setbacks as motivation to intensify foreign interventions—potentially renewing attacks on Iran, pressuring Ukraine regarding Russian demands, or revisiting global tariff policies.
items.title: Global Attention on U.S. Midterms Amid Trumpism Decline Concerns

items.summary: Diana Shnaider won the Pan Pacific Open singles title at Ariake Coliseum in Tokyo on Sunday, defeating Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 5-7, 6-2. The match lasted two hours and 19 minutes after Fernandez staged a comeback from 4-0 down in the second set before mounting an early decider break to take her first trophy of the 2026 season.
items.title: Shnaider Overcomes Collapse to Claim Pan Pacific Open Title

items.summary: Political theorist Wendy Brown discusses the significance of upcoming elections in Spain and the United States with EL PAÍS. She argues that liberal democracy is exhausted and cannot address climate or welfare challenges. According to her, neoliberalism reshapes social life beyond economics and hollows out democracy by reducing everything to economic value. Combined with fatalism about environmental disasters, this produces a nihilistic spiral she says has never been seen before. Brown calls for transforming the democratic system toward what she terms reparative democracy, based on caring for one another rather than individual interests.
items.title: Wendy Brown on neoliberalism, nihilism and reparative democracy

items.summary: A report titled 'Cuba: An island losing its people' describes ongoing emigration from Cuba, noting that families with children frequently queue at Havana's José Martí International Airport. A quoted airline employee said each week a classroom of schoolchildren leaves the country and every two months an entire school does. The article states Cuban migrants are now heading to Guyana before reaching Brazil, where they can legalize status and work; previously Nicaragua was used as a route toward the U. S. , estimated at around $10,000 per person. Figures from Cuba's National Office of Statistics and Information (ONEI) show an official population of 9,434,593 inhabitants in early 2026 versus 11,113,215 people in 2022, a deficit of 1,678,622 effective residents.
items.title: Cuba's Population Decline Driven by Emigration

items.summary: People evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky were reunited with family after crossing from Belarus into Ukraine on Saturday. Families gathered at a site in the Chernihiv region, arriving by bus and ambulance. They had previously travelled via Crimea and Russia following their Friday evacuation. The reunions coincide with a ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump that took effect across Kherson.
items.title: Oleshky evacuees reunited with loved ones in Chernihiv region

items.summary: Two cranberry bogs in Plymouth and Kingston, Massachusetts had been out of service for years because they were no longer financially viable. Distributed Energy Infrastructure announced the first-ever agrivoltaic cranberry harvests at these sites after DEI installed solar projects over them. Cranberry farmer Iain Ward was involved throughout design and construction to keep the wetland environment intact.
items.title: Solar Projects Restore Unprofitable Cranberry Bogs in Massachusetts

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that China's STAR50 index of AI and semiconductor companies collapsed about 40 percent over four months, wiping out $480 billion in market value. Citing Reuters through Futurism, the article frames this as evidence an AI bubble is bursting in China after similar speculation in the US. A Beijing fund manager told Reuters it had evolved into a speculative bull that is now deflating.
items.title: China's AI Bubble Deflates by Half a Trillion Dollars

items.summary: Elon Musk is considering merging electric vehicle maker Tesla and rocket manufacturer SpaceX under one corporate structure, a move that could create an entity worth nearly $3.5 trillion and reshape his technology empire. When asked whether the merger would make sense, Musk responded with an unequivocal "Yes." He noted there is no certainty a deal will occur and that shareholder approval plus regulatory hurdles remain. A combined valuation of approximately $3.5 trillion would rank among history's largest mergers. Potential benefits include cooperation on AI, chip design, robotics and satellite connectivity; challenges involve differing markets, national-security exposure and execution risk. The report draws partly on Reuters input.
items.title: Musk Weighs Tesla-SpaceX Merger Amid AI and Space Ambitions

items.summary: Union labour and employment minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched a verified WhatsApp service on Sunday, letting EPFO subscribers check their PF balance, view passbook details and see five recent transactions. The facility also offers guidance on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana and aims to cut office visits. It was unveiled at EPFO's 74th Foundation Day celebration.
items.title: EPFO Launches WhatsApp Services for Subscribers

items.summary: Temple founder Deepinder Goyal announced on Sunday that pre-orders for his health-tech wearable, Temple, are open, directing buyers to temple.com or the mobile app. The launch drew heavy traffic that temporarily disrupted the website before being resolved. Goyal shared results from an internal study comparing Temple's heart rate tracking against five flagship wearables—Apple Watch, WHOOP MG, Fitbit Air, Garmin FR970 and Oura Ring 5—using a taped Polar H10 chest strap as reference. He claimed Temple recorded the lowest error across all conditions, attributing its performance to adhesive attachment and placement over an artery near the temple. Early-access listings suggest a price of around Rs 85,000 including a lifetime subscription, though the company had not formally confirmed the final retail price in Sunday's announcement. An extended study by independent researchers is underway, which Goyal said he would fund.
items.title: Zomato Founder Opens Pre-orders for Temple Health Wearable

items.summary: A 63-year-old retired man from Kanjurmarg East says cyber fraudsters cheated him of Rs15.28 lakh after trapping him in a sextortion racket via a fake Facebook profile named Kajal Sharma. The accused recorded an obscene video, threatened to share it and impersonated police officers and YouTube officials demanding money for removals and post-mortem changes. He transferred the total from his and his wife's accounts before lodging a complaint with helpline 1930; police registered an FIR under BNS and IT Act sections while investigation continues.
items.title: Mumbai Retiree Loses Over Rs15 Lakh In Sextortion Scam

items.summary: Foreign affairs expert Waiel Awwad told ANI that a Republican victory in the US midterms could deliver significant negative impact for India through H-1B visa restrictions, tariff pressures and strict immigration curbs. He said President Donald Trump’s unilateral approach has already deviated from the strategic partnership between the two countries, even as America views India as indispensable in forums like the Quad and Indo-Pacific. Awwad noted surveys suggest Republicans may face setbacks amid rising fuel prices, which he put at USD 4.2 to USD 6.5, that have hurt American popularity.
items.title: Indian Expert Warns Trump Win Could Harm India on Visas, Tariffs

items.summary: Police said on Sunday that three people, including a woman, were arrested for allegedly writing pro-Khalistan slogans targeting singer Diljit Dosanjh at two Delhi Metro stations. The graffiti read
items.title: Three Arrested Over Pro-Khalistan Graffiti at Delhi Metro Stations After Diljit Concert

items.summary: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck of Bhutan dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa, number 76, to Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a ceremony on Sunday. The dedication occurred amid an event raising and consecrating 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City. King Wangchuck described the occasion as spiritually meaningful, reflecting Bhutan's Buddhist heritage and friendship between the two nations. Union minister Kiren Rijiju called it 'a huge honour' for India. Aryan Singh of The Times of India reported on the event from New Delhi. (59 words).
items.title: Bhutan's King Dedicates Buddhist Stupa to India's PM Modi in Gelephu Ceremony

items.summary: At its October 13 home product launch, Apple updated the Apple TV and introduced HomeView, a wall-mountable touchscreen hub that tilts on an aluminum base. The device marks a shift toward a reinvented Siri-led experience rather than an app-first ecosystem, borrowing personalization from iPhone proximity and drawing design cues from CarPlay. Unlike competitors' screens with cameras, HomeView has no dedicated app store or new homeOS.
items.title: Apple's HomeView Signals a Siri-First, Post-App Future for Smart Homes

items.summary: An 86-year-old CleanTechnica writer and his wife drove ~1500 miles from Northern Wisconsin to their home near Provo, Utah in a new 2026 Tesla Model Y running Full Self Driving V14.3.12 for the first time on a cross-country trip. They found FSD navigation occasionally led them astray at Superchargers and that charging was slower than with their older car; one stop used an old V2 charger limited to 50 kW, while another Hardware 4 charger reached ~100 kW. Most severely, FSD failed for nearly two days after a camera calibration glitch, forcing manual driving he called a strain at his age. He asks whether Tesla will refund the $99/month fee and reports current referral offers of three months free Full Self Driving plus Supercharging.
items.title: 86-Year-Old Couple Tests FSD on Cross-Country Road Trip

items.summary: National Grid agreed last week to buy 29.5 hectares (73 acres) at Dorman Point on land owned by the Teesworks partnership, moving toward Britain's biggest electricity substation near a planned AI datacentre. The deal may support up to 3.2GW of capacity as the UK expands its AI infrastructure amid strong public opposition and government policy statements stressing community benefits.
items.title: National Grid Secures Land for UK's Largest Substation Near Teesside Datacentre

items.summary: An Alaska judge dismissed a lawsuit backed by Donald Trump seeking to block certification of the state's US Senate race if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses. The justice department filed it in October, arguing two candidates named Dan Sullivan could confuse voters and help Democrat Mary Peltola. Sullivan said he would accept the results.
items.title: Alaska Judge Rejects Trump Bid To Block Senate Race Certification

items.summary: Haley Stevens, a former congresswoman who lost the Michigan Democratic nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his opponent Mike Rogers in a surprise appearance at a church. In a video posted to X, she said she no longer belonged in El-Sayed's campaign and criticized him for hate. The race is considered one of Tuesday's tightest Senate contests.
items.title: Michigan Democrat Endorses Republican Senate Candidate Amid Party Feud

items.summary: Investors withdrew $3.6bn from Binance as it recovered from a record hack in which billions were stolen Thursday, described as the biggest heist ever. The FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, linked to North Korea's Lazarus Group. Binance froze then phased withdrawals; by Sunday net outflow reached about $3.6bn (2.1% of its $171bn assets). It set aside $6.34bn and pledged full coverage as crypto prices fell.
items.title: Binance Reopens Withdrawals After Record North Korea–Linked Hack

items.summary: Heavily-armed officers have started patrolling Sydney's streets as part of heightened security following last year's deadly shooting at Bondi Beach. The Armed Response Command will deploy specially trained officers carrying long-arm rifles across busy tourist areas and major events, with New South Wales police describing the role as built on preserving life. Reactions are divided: one resident called the sight unnerving while another felt safer, Jewish communities welcomed it but Amnesty International Australia raised concerns about militarisation of policing.
items.title: Armed police begin patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack

items.summary: Interior ministers vowed tough penalties after overnight riots in Frankfurt left more than 100 police officers injured, with Roman Poseck of Hesse reporting that hooded rioters damaged 17 stores and 54 people were arrested. He said police estimate between 1,000 and 1,500 violent troublemakers are involved. Alexander Dobrindt warned perpetrators would be held to account while accusing immigrant-community members of acting with far-left groups without evidence.
items.title: German Ministers Promise Severe Penalties After Frankfurt Riots

items.summary: Champions Arsenal moved three points clear of the rest in the Premier League with Kai Havertz scoring an early goal to secure a 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, Nov. 1. Havertz tapped in from Declan Rice's low cross in the 16th minute after Liverpool were caught out trying to play out from the back.
items.title: Arsenal Claim Top Spot as Havertz Seals Win at Liverpool

items.summary: A wave of overnight freezer malfunctions at US military commissaries has prompted a possible cyberattack investigation, mirroring October's French supermarket hack that spoiled food worth millions. Pentagon officials say Cyber Command is coordinating with law enforcement but declined to elaborate; the Defense Criminal Investigative Service leads the probe. Investigators found temperature settings were raised and food melted or spoiled, though no link between the two incidents has been established.
items.title: US bases probe freezer failures after French attacks

items.summary: As Americans head to Tuesday's midterms, the Trump administration has compiled lists of possible noncitizen voters that could be used to contest election outcomes. The Justice Department acknowledged sending letters to officials in five states — California, Washington, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Nevada — as of October 30 about identifying noncitizens on voter rolls. A federal judge rejected its bid over the California list of about 20,000 voters on October 28, with an appeals court upholding that ruling on October 30. The administration says it will appeal to the Supreme Court and enforce the law wherever evidence leads. Legal experts say such challenges would face significant hurdles, partly because reviews found many listed people are US citizens.
items.title: Trump administration's noncitizen voter lists could challenge midterm results

items.summary: Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff face redundancy as the firm seeks to cut costs against billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition. The number is not finalised but likely a sizeable chunk of its 16,000 workforce, the BBC understands. VMO2 declined to comment. BT's share price jumped 7% after reports it was close to using Virgin Media O2's fibre network.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 faces thousands of job cuts amid debt and BT fibre deal

items.summary:
The government's CGFMU microloan guarantee scheme ended on March 31, 2026, raising uncertainty over risk pricing and unsecured lending. Banks such as IDFC First Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, Jana, Suryoday and Ujjivan had set aside the guarantee fee, expecting a reopening soon. Suryoday reported gross non-performing assets falling to 2.9% in September 2026 from 5.9% a year earlier. Analysts warn credit costs stay high without cover. Chief financial officers and managing directors said new disbursements would keep going under the programme once it reopens.

visual:null},
items.title: Banks Push for Extension of Microloan Guarantee Scheme

items.summary: Exit polls suggest Ilijana Yotova, the candidate of ruling centre-left party Progressive Bulgaria (PB), is set to win 52% of the vote in Bulgaria's presidential run-off election. Her pro-Western challenger Andrey Gyurov trails with around 45%, according to initial projections. Voter turnout stood at just 29%. If confirmed, Yotova would become Bulgaria's first elected female head of state.
items.title: Bulgaria's Exit Polls Point to Yotova in Presidential Runoff

items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads Formula 1 by a 123-point margin over teammate George Russell and a 124-point lead over Lewis Hamilton, with at most 125 points still available. He needs a 100-point-plus race result to become the youngest champion in history at this morning's Mexico City Grand Prix.
items.title: Antonelli on Brink of F1 Title as Race Runs in Mexico City

items.summary: Legendary Australian trainer Bart Cummings, known as the 'Cups King', won his tenth Melbourne Cup with Saintly in 1996. The chestnut gelding had a long stride suited to Flemington's straight course. Trackwork rider Joe Agresta observed Saintly run quicker times than expected during preparation races. Cummings adjusted his usual Derby Day plan, opting for the Cox Plate as lead-up instead of running on Derby Day. Jockey Darren Beadman shifted Saintly off the fence around 800m out and let him sprint clear near the finish line to clinch victory over Count Chivas and Skybeau. Agresta recalled Cummings's relief after winning with a horse he considered special, keeping Saintly at Princes Farm until his death in 2016.
items.title: Saintly's Melbourne Cup win and Bart Cummings's legendary training feat

items.summary: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, recorded net outflows of $3.6 billion after restoring customer withdrawals on Sunday following a cyber theft attributed by the FBI and blockchain analytics firms to North Korean hackers linked to TraderTraitor. The breach reportedly involved approximately $6.3 billion across 10 blockchains. Binance said it replaced about 95% of stolen assets using corporate treasury, emergency reserves and insurance funds, pledging that losses would not be passed on to users. Co-CEO Yi He noted some transfers were internal wallet movements. Despite the theft, withdrawals did not trigger a wider exodus; most major cryptocurrencies changed by less than 1%, with Bitcoin trading at approximately $78,000. (With Bloomberg inputs)
items.title: Binance Absorbs $6.3 Billion Hack Losses After Record Outflows

items.summary: India's opposition parties staged major protests in New Delhi on Sunday against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and a nationwide voter list review, which has fuelled demonstrations since the summer. The movement is led by the youth organization Cockroach Janta Party.
items.title: Thousands join Indian opposition protest

items.summary: On 1st November 2026, the site opened a discussion prompted by Kyle Kingsbury's Jepsen results for ParticleDB 1.1.4. It asks what maintainers can do to ensure correct software and accurate documentation when large language models erode trust in those products, and how they might then demonstrate quality to users. The piece frames LLMs as making the signals of a mature system easier to counterfeit, without attributing that view or offering solutions beyond the questions posed.
items.title: Kyle Kingsbury on Trust in LLM-Era Software and Documentation

items.summary: Carmakers reached new sales records in October as festive demand strengthened across categories. Maruti Suzuki led with domestic passenger vehicle sales rising 20.5% to 2,12,384 units, while Hyundai posted a record 62,799 units and Tata edged Mahindra's SUV record of 73,338 units by 556 vehicles. Growth spread across small cars, utility vehicles and electric models, though officials noted whether demand holds after the festive season remains to be seen.
items.title: Indian Carmakers Hit October Sales Records on Festive Demand

items.summary: The Punjab Police's Counter Intelligence wing arrested two people and seized 5 kg of heroin during a narcotics operation in Amritsar, the state Director General of Police said on Sunday. The Aam Aadmi Party praised the action as another major crackdown under Bhagwant Mann-led government.
items.title: Punjab Police Bust Heroin Smuggling Network in Amritsar

items.summary: The author argues that electric motorcycles will replace gasoline ones not by convincing current riders to switch but through generational replacement among younger people who grow up on electric two-wheelers. He says the conventional playbook of building a competitive and affordable electric version mirrors electric cars, which he rejects because for most Western riders especially Americans a motorcycle is passion rather than transportation tied to its engine character. Harley-Davidson’s 2018 LiveWire release illustrates this: despite rave reviews it sold poorly partly at $30,000 but mainly because it could not satisfy the gasoline itch of traditional owners. He notes many years were wasted on conversion attempts and forecasts a gradual transition as older enthusiasts age out while solid-state batteries improve range and fueling time so electrics become the only comfortable option for new riders. He concludes gasoline motorcycles will fade with their customers rather than lose at performance, paraphrasing T. S.
items.title: Electric Motorcycles Win Through Generational Replacement, Not Conversion

items.summary: Cyclone Murasu is approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast days after Cyclone Arnab struck the state. Authorities are evacuating residents from unsafe areas and deploying disaster response teams while relief operations continue in both Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring Odisha. The IMD expects Murasu to make landfall near Ongole late Monday night or early Tuesday, with winds of 100–110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph. Around 1.18 lakh people remain affected by Arnab’s floods as further rain threatens recovery efforts through November 4. Chennai has declared a school holiday on November 2 amid heavy rainfall forecasts.
items.title: Murasu Approaches Andhra, Odisha as Relief Continues After Arnab

items.summary: This Euronews news bulletin, dated November 1st, 2026 evening, offers a roundup of the most important stories from around Europe and beyond. The newsroom delivers updates on world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel within just a few minutes. Reported with independence and a European perspective, this regular round-up provides viewers with a clear overview of current events.
items.title: Euronews Broadcasts Evening News Roundup Across Europe and Beyond

items.summary: Simon Farley, a history lecturer at The University of Melbourne writing for The Conversation, argues the common myna is unfairly vilified as 'Australia's most hated bird'. He notes the species has been in Victoria since 1862 and Queensland since 1883. Public attitudes shifted from praise to hatred by the 1980s amid backlash against invasive species. Farley contends the birds have not changed, only perceptions of them. He warns that trapping programs may create an illusion of success while allowing other species like the noisy miner to fill gaps, and cautions many efforts fight 'an unwinnable war', suggesting observation over eradication.
items.title: Historian questions Australia's war on mynas

items.summary: Peterbilt is adding its medium- and heavy-duty battery electric trucks to the cooperative purchasing agreement with government procurement consortium Sourcewell, extending through 2028. The change gives Sourcewell’s more than 50,000 member organizations access to competitively solicited contracts with pre-negotiated pricing across Class 5-8 trucks, potentially eliminating lengthy bidding processes for eligible agencies. Erik Johnson of Peterbilt said the move reflects its commitment to public fleets.
items.title: Peterbilt Adds Electric Trucks to Sourcewell Government Fleet Purchasing Agreement

items.summary: Food safety authorities in Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district seized over 22,000 litres of suspected adulterated and expired ghee worth around ₹1.6 crore during raids at two establishments on Saturday, police said on Sunday. The joint team recovered a total of 22,138 litres from Ananya Trading Company's warehouse and factory, where officials found the product packed under brand names including Trisalwa, Bansuri, Shrinand and Mayra. Preliminary questioning suggested expired ghee was repackaged with fresh labels before sale, and investigators suspect palm oil and vanaspati sourced from Gujarat were used to prepare it.
items.title: Rajasthan Seizes Adulterated Expired Ghee Worth Crore, Arrests Three

items.summary: In Panchkula, Haryana, an eight-year-old boy allegedly lured a six-year-old girl into an empty classroom and assaulted her before leading her unconscious father there. The incident occurred on October 28 between 3 pm and 4 pm at Sector 20 school. Hindustan Times could not independently verify the video showing the assault. Two JBT teachers were suspended, and police registered an FIR against the school management for negligence.
items.title: Panchkula boy led victim's father to bloodied classroom after assault

items.summary: The United States is racing to reestablish itself as a frontrunner in the global nuclear energy sector, even though it remains the world’s largest producer but may lose that status soon because China has outspent it on research and development for years. Analyst Damien Ma of Gavekal Technologies wrote via the South China Morning Post that “By a wide margin, China will have the world’s most dynamic and significant nuclear industry through 2035.” In response, researchers at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory announced they developed an alloy called V555 that withstood stresses of up to 600 megapascals (MPa) at room temperature. Critics caution that focusing on futuristic technologies may be misguided rather than revitalizing the sector.
items.title: U.S. Labs Pursue New Materials to Counter China's Nuclear Lead

items.summary: On Lomé Beach, Anthony Yao Sodjinê prepares for a match of sambo, a Soviet-era discipline now gaining ground in West Africa. Since June 2024 the Togolese Sambo Federation has organized demonstrations there; its first event is the Africa Initiative Cup. A memorandum signed in April 2023 by Russian and Togolese sports ministers covers school sport, infrastructure and training. Andrey Belogonov says it could open scholarships to Russia, while Gneny Tchagbele confirms Togo will participate.
items.title: Togo and Russia deepen ties through sambo in Lomé

items.summary: A 21-year-old man accused of attacking a Class 10 girl with a chainsaw at Rapthadu ZP school in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, was shot by police on Sunday night while allegedly fleeing custody. He hurled stones as officers escorted him for a crime scene reconstruction; several were injured and he fired six rounds before being hospitalized in serious condition.
items.title: Accused of chainsaw attack shot by police during scene reconstruction
